===PAGE 146=== (ocr, 55 lines)
   1|                        Section 3: Designation of Architectural Preservation District (APD)
   2|                        The APD shall, by Town Meeting vote, encompass the areas shown on the map entitled "Town of Lunenburg, Architectural
   3|                        Preservation District," and appended to this bylaw. Amendments to the district boundaries may be made only by vote of
   4|                        Town Meeting.
   5|                        Section 4: Architectural Preservation District Commission (APDC)
   6|                        The Board of Selectmen shall appoint a five-member APD to oversee the APD pursuant to this bylaw. Initially, two
   7|                       members shall be appointed for one year, two for two years, and one for three years; each successive appointment shall be
   8|                       made for three years. The Board of Selectmen may also appoint up to two alternate members, initially for terms of one, two
   9|                       and three years, and for three-year terms thereafter. If members are absent, unable to act, or recused from voting due to a
  10|                       conflict of interest, the APDC chair may designate one or both of the alternate members to serve in their place. To the extent
  11|                       achievable, the APDC shall be comprised of the following persons: a member of the Lunenburg Historical Commission; a
  12|                        design professional; a craftsperson or building contractor familiar with historic restoration; and two residents of the APD and
  13|                       one resident at large. Members and alternates of the APDC shall by reason of experience and/or education have
  14|                       demonstrable knowledge, interest, and ability to effectively carry out the APDC's responsibilities.
  15|                        Section 5: APDC Powers and Duties
  16|                        The APDC shall exercise its powers in reviewing the alteration (substantial or minor), including demolition of contributing
  17|                       properties within the APD as set forth in this bylaw, and in accordance with the standards described in Section 9. Within 180
  18|                       days of its establishment, the APDC shall adopt design guidelines to assist the APDC in determining whether the proposal
  19|                        satisfies the standards described in Section 9, as well as to facilitate owner understanding of, and compliance with, those
  20|                        standards. The APDC may also promulgate rules and regulations consistent with the provisions of this bylaw, or set forth
  21|                       such forms and procedures as it deems appropriate for the regulation of its affairs and the conduct of its business, including
  22|                       requirements for the contents and form of applications for certificates, hearing procedures and other matters. In adopting
  23|                       design guidelines and rules and regulations, including any subsequent amendments, the APDC shall first hold a duly posted
  24|                       public hearing advertised at least fourteen (14) days in advance within a newspaper of local circulation.
  25|                       The APDC shall not adopt or amend any design guidelines or rules and regulations until at least 35 days after the APDC has
  26|                       provided a copy of those proposed guidelines or rules and regulations to the Board of Selectmen.
  27|                       Section 6: Exemptions
  28|                        The following are exempt from the requirements of this bylaw:
  29|                       a) Routine maintenance of Contributing Properties.
  30|                       b) Repairs or improvements which do not require a building permit from the Building Inspector.
  31|                       c) Temporary buildings (subject to time and size limits imposed by the APDC).
  32|                       d) Interior building alterations.
  33|                       e) Exterior building colors.
  34|                       f) Installation, removal or replacement of storm windows and storm doors, screen windows and screen doors.
  35|                       g) Installation, removal or replacement of gutters, downspouts, window shutters and door shutters.
  36|                       h) Structures not defined as Contributing Properties.
  37|                        Section 7: Administrative Review/Determination of Applicability
  38|                       Minor alterations such as like for like replacement of architectural features and other minor work (as outlined in the APDC
  39|                       regulations) shall be reviewed through this process to ensure consistency of the property's character and appropriateness of
  40|                       the proposed materials. The APDC shall make a determination that the proposed work is exempt or that it does not retain the
  41|                       character of the Contributing Property. In the case where the work does not retain the character of the Contributing Property
  42|                       it shall be determined to equate to a substantial alteration and require a binding review per Section 8 of this Bylaw.
  43|                        Property owners considering substantial alterations to a Contributing Property are strongly encouraged, but not required, to
  44|                       request an Administrative Review from the APDC. This review would focus on directing the applicant toward developing a
  45|                        proposal that would be compliant with the Binding Review Process in Section 8.
  46|                        Administrative Review does not require a public hearing and can be requested electronically. In providing Administrative
  47|                        Review for a proposed Alteration, the APDC shall make a finding as to whether or not the proposed Alteration is compatible
  48|                        with the standards in Section 9 and the associated design guidelines. The APDC shall provide its finding in writing, as a
  49|                        Negative Determination or a Requirement of Binding Review, and within 45 days of receiving a request for Administrative
  50|                        Review. The Requirement of Binding Review may include recommendations on how the proposed Alteration could be made
  51|                        more consistent with the standards and the design guidelines.
  52|                        Section 8: Binding Review
  53|                        The following Alterations require the submittal of an application for binding review by the APDC:
  54|                       (a) Demolition of all or a part of a Contributing Property.
  55|                                                                                                    146

===PAGE 147=== (ocr, 56 lines)
   1|                       (b) Substantial Alterations to a Contributing Property.
   2|                       Applications should include a completed application form and photographs showing existing buildings and site conditions.
   3|                       For substantial alteration, including additions and demolition, applicants should also provide building elevations showing the
   4|                       proposed configuration and building materials; a plan showing the approximate footprint and relationships of buildings to
   5|                       other structures, exterior circulation, and points of entry; and any other plans which may help to demonstrate the proposed
   6|                       building design. Applications can be submitted electronically, but applicants shall also provide one hard copy of the
   7|                       application to the Planning Office. If appropriate, the APDC may waive any or all of the requirements for design submittal
   8|                       and review.
   9|                       Within forty-five (45) days of the application submittal, a copy of which shall be filed with the Town Clerk, the APDC shall
  10|                       hold a public hearing on the application, said hearing to be noticed by an ad published at least once in a newspaper with local
  11|                       circulation fourteen (14) days or more before the hearing. Following the hearing, the APDC shall determine whether or not
  12|                       the proposed Alteration is consistent with the standards set forth in Section 9 and the associated design guidelines. If the
  13|                       APDC determines by majority vote that the Alteration adheres to the standards and the design guidelines, it shall issue a
  14|                       Certificate to Alter, which may be subject to reasonable conditions that the APDC deems necessary and appropriate. If the
  15|                       APDC does not achieve a majority vote that the Alteration is compatible with the standards and the design guidelines, it shall
  16|                       make a negative determination. The APDC's written determination shall be submitted to the property owner within twenty
  17|                       (20) days of the close of the public hearing, and no later than ninety (90) days after the submittal of an application, unless
  18|                       granted a time extension by the owner. In making its determination, the APDC shall provide a rationale for its action,
  19|                       including a description of how the alteration does or does not meet the standards set forth in Section 9 and the design
  20|                       guidelines. If the APDC denies a Certificate to Alter, it may include non-binding advisory only, recommendations on how
  21|                       the proposed Alterations may be modified to satisfy the APDC. Once the applicant modifies the Alterations in a manner that
  22|                       the APDC finds acceptable, the APDC shall issue a Certificate to Alter. The determinations of the APDC relative to
  23|                       Alterations described in this Section 8, whether positive or negative, shall be binding on the applicant.
  24|                       Section 9: Design Standards When reviewing an application, the APDC shall consider the following standards, which are
  25|                       intended to guide the property owner in the site development and building design, as well as the APDC in its review of
  26|                       proposed actions as described in Section 8 above:
  27|                       (a) Height and Proportions - The height, proportions, and relationship of height to width between windows, doors, signs
  28|                       and other architectural elements should be compatible with the architectural style and character of the building or structure.
  29|                       (b) Relation of Structures and Spaces - The relation of a structure to the open space between it and adjoining structures
  30|                       should be compatible with such relationships in the district.
  31|                       (c) Shape - The shape of roofs, windows, doors and other design elements should be compatible with the architectural style
  32|                       and character of the building.
  33|                       (d) Scale - The scale of a structure alteration should be compatible with its architectural design style and character and that of
  34|                       the district.
  35|                       (e) Directional Expression - Building facades and other architectural design elements should be compatible with those of
  36|                       others in the district with regard to the dominant vertical or horizontal expression or direction related to use and historical or
  37|                       cultural character, as appropriate.
  38|                       (f) Garages and Accessory Buildings - Garages and accessory buildings shall be sensitively integrated into the overall
  39|                       development, and should not be the predominant design feature when viewed from the street.
  40|                      (g) Materials & Methods of Construction - Materials used shall be consistent with the appearance and character of the
  41|                       surrounding properties and contribute to historic nature of the area. Construction methods shall meet Building Code
  42|                       requirements and visually resemble historic patterns but may use contemporary technology.
  43|                       Section 10: Procedures for Issuance and Filing of APDC Determinations: Each Certificate to Alter or negative
  44|                       determination issued by the APDC shall be dated and signed by its chair or such other person designated by the APDC to
  45|                       sign certificates on its behalf. The APDC shall send a written copy of its actions to the property owner and shall file other
  46|                       copies with the office of the Town Clerk and the Building Inspector. The date of issuance of a certificate or negative
  47|                       determination shall be the date of its filing of other said copy with the office of the Town Clerk. If the APDC should fail to
  48|                       submit a written determination within twenty (20) days of closing its public hearing, or within ninety (90) days of the
  49|                       submittal of a Certificate, or within such further time as the applicant may allow in writing, a Certificate to Alter shall be
  50|                       waived in favor of the property owner.
  51|                       Section 11: Enforcement In addition to the duties previously set forth in this Bylaw, the APDC or the Building Inspector
  52|                       shall issue enforcement orders, with an immediate cease and desist order directing compliance with this Bylaw and shall
  53|                       undertake any other enforcement authorized by law.
  54|                       Upon request of APDC, and with the approval of the Board of Selectmen, the Town Counsel shall take legal action on behalf
  55|                       of the Town for enforcement of this Bylaw, or any order issued hereunder, in any court of competent jurisdiction.
  56|                                                                                                    147

===PAGE 148=== (ocr, 47 lines)
   1|                       In the case of demolition, including demolition by neglect, without approval of the APDC no building permit shall be issued
   2|                       with respect to any Contributing Property within the APD that caused a demolition of its building, structure or Contributing
   3|                       Property for a period of up to two (2) years after the date of the violation.
   4|                       The APDC or its designee may use any and all of the aforementioned enforcement methods to address the contributing
   5|                       factors of demolition by neglect for purposes of preventing a Contributing Property from becoming structurally deficient or
   6|                       economically infeasible to repair.
   7|                       Section 12: Coordination with Other Town Boards and Bylaws
   8|                       (a) Except as stated in "(b)" below, the APDC's authority as established in this bylaw shall not supersede or interfere with the
   9|                       regulatory authority of other local or state boards or APDCs.
  10|                       (b) By exercise of this bylaw, the APDC assumes the authority of the Lunenburg Historical Commission pursuant to Chapter
  11|                       XVI of these General Bylaws, relative to the proposed demolition (including demolition by neglect) of buildings that are over
  12|                       75 years of age and located within the APD.
  13|                       (c) The APDC shall coordinate its review with that of other Town Boards.
  14|                       (d) The APDC shall be included as an advisory review entity in new construction projects that move through the Planning
  15|                       Board Development Plan Review and/or Special Permit processes.
  16|                       Section 13: Appeal Procedure
  17|                       Any aggrieved party may appeal the action of the APDC in accordance with the General Laws.
  18|                       Section 14: Validity and Separability
  19|                       The provisions of this bylaw shall be deemed to be separable. If any of its provisions, sections, subsections, sentences or
  20|                       clauses shall be held to be invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this bylaw
  21|                       shall continue to be in full force and effect.
  22|                       Section 15: Appendices
  23|                       Appendix A: The location and boundaries of the Town of Lunenburg Architectural Preservation District are defined and
  24|                       shown on the Town of Lunenburg Village Center District Map and the Town of Lunenburg Historic District Map, which is a
  25|                       part of this bylaw." or take any other action relative thereto. (Submitted by the Historical Commission and the Planning

  28|                       ARTICLE 26. VOTED (with amendments italicized) to amend the General Bylaws of the Town by adding
  29|                       Section XXXII, entitled Architectural Preservation District, as follows:
  30|                       Section XXXII ARCHITECTURAL PRESERVATION DISTRICT
  31|                       Section 1: Purpose
  32|                       This bylaw is enacted under the Home Rule Amendment of the Massachusetts Constitution for the purposes of:
  33|                       (a) Preserving, restoring and protecting groups of historically and/or architecturally significant buildings and the
  34|                       characteristics of their neighborhoods that are important to the town's architectural, cultural, economic, political and/or social
  35|                       history;
  36|                       (b) Fostering wider public knowledge and appreciation of such neighborhoods and Contributing Properties;
  37|                       (c) Limiting the detrimental effect of alterations (substantial & minor), additions, and demolitions on the character of such
  38|                       Contributing Properties and their neighborhood settings;
  39|                       (d) Reviewing proposed alterations (substantial and minor) including demolition of or to any Contributing Property located
  40|                       within the APD, for appropriateness and compatibility with the existing buildings, setting and neighborhood character; and
  41|                       (e) Facilitating the protection of the APD through a regulatory review.
  42|                       To achieve these purposes, the Town of Lunenburg may designate APDs to be administered as set forth in this bylaw.
  43|                       Section 2: Definitions
  44|                       For the purpose of this bylaw, the terms and words listed below shall have the following meaning:
  45|                       ADDITION: Any addition to a principal or accessory Contributing Property that is enclosed by walls and which increases
  46|                       the existing gross floor area.

  12|                       f) Installation, removal or replacement of storm windows and storm doors, screen windows and screen doors.
  13|                       g) Installation, removal or replacement of gutters, downspouts, window shutters and door shutters.
  14|                       h) Structures not defined as Contributing Properties.
  15|                       Section 7: Administrative Review/Determination of Applicability
  16|                       Minor alterations such as like for like replacement of architectural features and other minor work (as outlined in the APDC
  17|                       regulations) shall be reviewed through this process to ensure consistency of the property's character and appropriateness of
  18|                       the proposed materials. The APDC shall make a determination that the proposed work is exempt or that it does not retain the
  19|                       character of the Contributing Property. In the case where the work does not retain the character of the Contributing Property
  20|                       it shall be determined to equate to a substantial alteration and require a binding review per Section 8 of this Bylaw.
  21|                       Property owners considering substantial alterations to a Contributing Property are strongly encouraged, but not required, to
  22|                       request an Administrative Review from the APDC. This review would focus on directing the applicant toward developing a
  23|                       proposal that would be compliant with the Binding Review Process in Section 8. Administrative Review does not require a
  24|                       public hearing and can be requested electronically. In providing Administrative Review for a proposed Alteration, the APDC
  25|                       shall make a finding as to whether or not the proposed Alteration is compatible with the standards in Section 9 and the
  26|                       associated design guidelines. The APDC shall provide its finding in writing, as a Negative Determination or a Requirement
  27|                       of Binding Review, and within 45 days of receiving a request for Administrative Review. The Requirement of Binding
  28|                       Review may include recommendations on how the proposed Alteration could be made more consistent with the standards and
  29|                       the design guidelines.
  30|                       Section 8: Binding Review
  31|                       The following Alterations require the submittal of an application for binding review by the APDC:
  32|                       (a) Demolition of all or a part of a Contributing Property.
  33|                       (b) Substantial Alterations to a Contributing Property.
  34|                        Applications should include a completed application form and photographs showing existing buildings and site conditions.
  35|                       For substantial alteration, including additions and demolition, applicants should also provide building elevations showing the
  36|                       proposed configuration and building materials; a plan showing the approximate footprint and relationships of buildings to
  37|                       other structures, exterior circulation, and points of entry; and any other plans which may help to demonstrate the proposed
  38|                       building design. Applications can be submitted electronically, but applicants shall also provide one hard copy of the
  39|                       application to the Planning Office. If appropriate, the APDC may waive any or all of the requirements for design submittal
  40|                        Within thirty (45) days of the application submittal, a copy of which shall be filed with the Town Clerk, the APDC shall hold
  41|                       a public hearing on the application, said hearing to be noticed by an ad published at least once in a newspaper with local
  42|                       circulation fourteen (14) days or more before the hearing. Following the hearing, the APDC shall determine whether or not
  43|                       the proposed Alteration is consistent with the standards set forth in Section 9 and the associated design guidelines. If the
  44|                        APDC determines by majority vote that the Alteration adheres to the standards and the design guidelines, it shall issue a
  45|                       Certificate to Alter, which may be subject to reasonable conditions that the APDC deems necessary and appropriate. If the
  46|                        APDC does not achieve a majority vote that the Alteration is compatible with the standards and the design guidelines, it shall
  47|                       make a negative determination. The APDC's written determination shall be submitted to the property owner within twenty
  48|                       (20) days of the close of the public hearing, and no later than ninety (90) days after the submittal of an application, unless
  49|                       granted a time extension by the owner. In making its determination, the APDC shall provide a rationale for its action,
  50|                       including a description of how the alteration does or does not meet the standards set forth in Section 9 and the design
  51|                       guidelines. If the APDC denies a Certificate to Alter, it may include non- binding advisory only, recommendations on how
  52|                       the proposed Alterations may be modified to satisfy the APDC. Once the applicant modifies the Alterations in a manner that
  53|                       the APDC finds acceptable, the APDC shall issue a Certificate to Alter. The determinations of the APDC relative to
  54|                        Alterations described in this Section 8, whether positive or negative, shall be binding on the applicant.
  55|                                                                                                    152

===PAGE 153=== (ocr, 54 lines)
   1|                       Section 9: Design Standards When reviewing an application, the APDC shall consider the following standards, which are
   2|                       intended to guide the property owner in the site development and building design, as well as the APDC in its review of
   3|                       proposed actions as described in Section 8 above:
   4|                       (a) Height and Proportions - The height, proportions, and relationship of height to width between windows, doors, signs
   5|                       and other architectural elements should be compatible with the architectural style and character of the building or structure.
   6|                       (b) Relation of Structures and Spaces - The relation of a structure to the open space between it and adjoining structures
   7|                       should be compatible with such relationships in the district.
   8|                       (c) Shape - The shape of roofs, windows, doors and other design elements should be compatible with the architectural style
   9|                       and character of the building.
  10|                       (d) Scale - The scale of a structure alteration should be compatible with its architectural design style and character and that of
  11|                       the district.
  12|                       (e) Directional Expression - Building facades and other architectural design elements should be compatible with those of
  13|                       others in the district with regard to the dominant vertical or horizontal expression or direction related to use and historical or
  14|                       cultural character, as appropriate.
  15|                       (f) Garages and Accessory Buildings — Garages and accessory buildings shall be sensitively integrated into the overall
  16|                       development, and should not be the predominant design feature when viewed from the street.
  17|                       (g) Materials & Methods of Construction - Materials used shall be consistent with the appearance and character of the
  18|                       surrounding properties and contribute to historic nature of the area. Construction methods shall meet Building Code
  19|                       requirements and visually resemble historic patterns but may use contemporary technology.
  20|                       Section 10: Procedures for Issuance and Filing of APDC Determinations: Each Certificate to Alter or negative
  21|                       determination issued by the APDC shall be dated and signed by its chair or such other person designated by the APDC to
  22|                       sign certificates on its behalf. The APDC shall send a written copy of its actions to the property owner and shall file other
  23|                       copies with the office of the Town Clerk and the Building Inspector. The date of issuance of a certificate or negative
  24|                       determination shall be the date of its filing of other said copy with the office of the Town Clerk. If the APDC should fail to
  25|                       submit a written determination within twenty (20) days of closing its public hearing, or within ninety (90) days of the
  26|                       submittal of a Certificate, or within such further time as the applicant may allow in writing, a Certificate to Alter shall be
  27|                       waived in favor of the property owner.
  28|                       Section 11: Enforcement In addition to the duties previously set forth in this Bylaw, the APDC or the Building Inspector
  29|                       shall issue enforcement orders, with an immediate cease and desist order directing compliance with this Bylaw and shall
  30|                       undertake any other enforcement authorized by law.
  31|                       Upon request of APDC, and with the approval of the Board of Selectmen, the Town Counsel shall take legal action on behalf
  32|                       of the Town for enforcement of this Bylaw, or any order issued hereunder, in any court of competent jurisdiction.
  33|                       In the case of demolition, including demolition by neglect, without approval of the APDC no building permit shall be issued
  34|                       with respect to any Contributing Property within the APD that caused a demolition of its building, structure or Contributing
  35|                       Property for a period of up to two (2) years after the date of the violation.
  36|                       The APDC or its designee may use any and all of the aforementioned enforcement methods to address the contributing
  37|                       factors of demolition by neglect for purposes of preventing a Contributing Property from becoming structurally de ficient or
  38|                       economically infeasible to repair.
  39|                       Section 12: Coordination with Other Town Boards and Bylaws
  40|                       (a) Except as stated in "(b)" below, the APDC's authority as established in this bylaw shall not supersede or interfere with the
  41|                       regulatory authority of other local or state boards or APDCs.
  42|                       (b) By exercise of this bylaw, the APDC assumes the authority of the Lunenburg Historical Commission pursuant to Chapter
  43|                       XVI of these General Bylaws, relative to the proposed demolition (including demolition by neglect) of buildings that are over
  44|                       75 years of age and located within the APD.
  45|                       (c) The APDC shall coordinate its review with that of other Town Boards.
  46|                       (d) The APDC shall be included as an advisory review entity in new construction projects that move through the Planning
  47|                       Board Development Plan Review and/or Special Permit processes.
  48|                       Section 13: Appeal Procedure
  49|                        Any aggrieved party may appeal the action of the APDC in accordance with the General Laws.
  50|                       Section 14: Validity and Separability
  51|                       The provisions of this bylaw shall be deemed to be separable. If any of its provisions, sections, subsections, sentences or
  52|                       clauses shall be held to be invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction, the remainder of this bylaw
  53|                       shall continue to be in full force and effect.

   5|                        ARTICLE 27. To see if the Town will vote to amend the Zoning Bylaw by adding Section 4.17, Village Center
   6|                       District as follows:
   7|                       4.17. VILLAGE CENTER DISTRICT
   8|                       PREAMBLE
   9|                       The Lunenburg Town Center region has tremendous importance in symbolizing the unique character and heritage of
  10|                       Lunenburg. As residents engage with the historic buildings and streetscape of this area in the course of their routine daily
  11|                       business, be it school related, recreational, commercial, or even just driving through, the experience greatly reinforces a
  12|                       profound bond with the town's present community and past heritage.
  13|                       There is an opportunity to significantly improve the quality of this already poignant civic experience and increase the number
  14|                       of people who will be drawn to share in it by expanding the businesses and other attractions in the area. There is also a key
  15|                       challenge to preserving this critical embodiment of our town. Appropriate new uses or remedies must be found to the
  16|                       increasing number of underutilized buildings located about the town center.
  17|                       Town planning experience and best practices, as exemplified in the state's model bylaw for Village Center Districts,
  18|                       demonstrates some key ingredients to sustaining and enriching this type of environment in small towns. One of these is
  19|                       careful stewardship through clear guidelines for development consistent with what the area means to the community.
  20|                        Another is encouraging a level of intensive mixed use development, so that the critical mass of social and economic activity
  21|                       can be reached that will naturally provide the resources and inspiration required to maintain and organically adapt the area
  22|                       landmarks, buildings, and infrastructure without excessive burden on the Town's public finances.
  23|                       4.17.1. Purpose
  24|                       In pursuit of this opportunity and to address this challenge, the Town implements this bylaw and designates this zoning
  25|                       district as Village Center District in order to encourage economic and residential growth that fits the character of the Town.
  26|                       The purposes of the Village Center District are to:
  27|                       a. Build upon the historic development patterns in the existing village centers to create attractive, walkable neighborhoods;
  28|                       b. Encourage adaptive reuse of abandoned, vacant or underutilized buildings or structures where appropriate;
  29|                       c. Allow for a mix of new land uses that are appropriate to both the needs of the community and the scale of surrounding
  30|                       neighborhoods;
  31|                       d. Provide incentives to develop larger parcels at higher densities and in a coordinated, planned approach;
  32|                       e. Maintain a consistently high level of design quality throughout the district;
  33|                       f. Encourage the development of mixed use buildings and campuses that are designed and constructed in a manner that is
  34|                       contextually sensitive to the existing structures and facilities.
  35|                       4.17.2. Establishment
  36|                       The Village Center District is hereby established as of 1 January 2016 and consists of the area shown as the Village Center
  37|                       District on Town of Lunenburg Zoning Map on file with the Town/City Clerk and dated 2 May 2015 as may be amended
  38|                       from time to time by Town Meeting.
  39|                       4.17.3. Definitions
  40|                       Artist Space: A shop for the creation and/or sale of goods made by a potter, ceramicist, silversmith, jewelry maker, painter,
  41|                       photographer or other fine artist. This space may also serve as a living space for the artist provided there is adequate
  42|                       separation between uses per the governing Building and Health Codes.
  43|                       Banner: A strip of cloth or other man made fabric on which a sign is painted, silk-screened or printed. The display area shall
  44|                       be defined as the area of one face of the banner. The banner shall not exceed (40) square feet and shall not be displayed for
  45|                       more than fourteen (14) consecutive days.
  46|                        Bed & Breakfast: Bed and Breakfast, or Bed and Breakfast Establishment provided that:
  47|                       a) The dwelling is owner occupied.
  48|                       b) The lot conforms to all dimensional requirements of the Zoning Bylaw.
  49|                       c) Parking for each room available for rent is provided in the side yard behind the setback line or in the rear yard, but not
  50|                       nearer than ten (10) feet to any property line. One (1) parking place shall be provided for each bedroom.
  51|                       d) The outside appearance of the building is not altered from that of a residence, except to comply with the Building Code.
  52|                                                                                                    154

   1|                       Civic Use: A land use that provides a public, cultural, or institutional benefit to the community. Specific uses may include,
   2|                       but shall not be limited to, government offices, religious institutions, educational institutions, and medical facilities (not
   3|                       including veterinary operations). For the purposes of this bylaw, civic uses shall not include open space as defined below.
   4|                       Multiple Commercial Use: A combination of commercial uses within a single building or lot. In the case of uses that fall
   5|                       under the Special Permit requirements of Section 4.17.5.b. a Zoning Board of Appeals decision must be rendered on the use
   6|                       prior to the filing for Development Plan Review.
   7|                       Mixed Use: A combination of commercial and residential uses within a single building or lot. In the case of uses that fall
   8|                       under the Special Permit requirements of Section 4.17.5.b. a Zoning Board of Appeals decision must be rendered on the use
   9|                       prior to the filing for Development Plan Review.
  10|                       Personal Service: An establishment engaged in the provision of services to the general public which are conducted within the
  11|                       structure. This includes, but is not limited to, barbers, hair salons, massage therapists, chiropractors and nail salons.
  12|                       Professional Office: An office primarily devoted to professional activities, including, but not limited to, banks, real estate,
  13|                       insurance or other agency offices; an office of an accountant, physician, teacher, dentist, engineer, lawyer, homebuilder,
  14|                       photographer, or other recognized professional for which specific training and/or licensing is required. Drive-thru service
  15|                       shall be limited to banks and shall require a Special Permit.
  16|                       Open Space: In the context of an application for a Village Center District Special Permit, this term denotes open areas set
  17|                       aside for public use as part of a coordinated site development process. Specific requirements for ownership and maintenance
  18|                       are provided in Section 4.17.9. and shall not include areas covered with impervious surface treatments.
  19|                       Transparency: The amount of transparent space that occupies a building façade including standard street-level windows and
  20|                       doorway windows.
  21|                       Restaurant: A place serving food and beverage within a structure or patio, primarily for consumption on the premises. Drive-
  22|                       thru windows shall be prohibited for this use.
  23|                       Retail: An establishment engaged in displaying and selling goods or merchandise within a building to the general public or
  24|                       to business establishments where the goods or merchandise are not intended for resale. There shall be no outdoor display of
  25|                       goods without the granting of Special Permit from the Board of Appeals.

  34|                                 (4.5) square feet to display the company or agency name.
  35|                       3) Site Design
  36|                          i.      Buildings shall be arranged in a manner that optimizes the ability of residents and consumers to access public spaces
  37|                                   (iii) Open space provided pursuant to Section 4.17.9.b. of this bylaw shall be designed as a public gathering place.

  43|                                  lighting, shade trees, perennial gardens, picnic areas, and/or trash receptacles.

===PAGE 160=== (ocr, 42 lines)
   1|                       4.17. VILLAGE CENTER DISTRICT
   2|                       PREAMBLE
   3|                       The Lunenburg Town Center region has tremendous importance in symbolizing the unique character and heritage of
   4|                       Lunenburg. As residents engage with the historic buildings and streetscape of this area in the course of their routine daily
   5|                       business, be it school related, recreational, commercial, or even just driving through, the experience greatly reinforces a
   6|                       profound bond with the town's present community and past heritage.
   7|                       There is an opportunity to significantly improve the quality of this already poignant civic experience and increase the number
   8|                       of people who will be drawn to share in it by expanding the businesses and other attractions in the area. There is also a key
   9|                       challenge to preserving this critical embodiment of our town. Appropriate new uses or remedies must be found to the
  10|                       increasing number of underutilized buildings located about the town center.
  11|                       Town planning experience and best practices, as exemplified in the state's model bylaw for Village Center Districts,
  12|                       demonstrates some key ingredients to sustaining and enriching this type of environment in small towns. One of these is
  13|                       careful stewardship through clear guidelines for development consistent with what the area means to the community.
  14|                        Another is encouraging a level of intensive mixed use development, so that the critical mass of social and economic activity
  15|                       can be reached that will naturally provide the resources and inspiration required to maintain and organically adapt the area
  16|                       landmarks, buildings, and infrastructure without excessive burden on the Town's public finances.
  17|                       4.17.1. Purpose
  18|                       In pursuit of this opportunity and to address this challenge, the Town implements this bylaw and designates this zoning
  19|                       district as Village Center District in order to encourage economic and residential growth that fits the character of the Town.
  20|                       The purposes of the Village Center District are to:
  21|                       a. Build upon the historic development patterns in the existing village centers to create attractive, walkable neighborhoods;
  22|                       b. Encourage adaptive reuse of abandoned, vacant or underutilized buildings or structures where appropriate;
  23|                       c. Allow for a mix of new land uses that are appropriate to both the needs of the community and the scale of surrounding
  24|                       neighborhoods;
  25|                       d. Provide incentives to develop larger parcels at higher densities and in a coordinated, planned approach;
  26|                       e. Maintain a consistently high level of design quality throughout the district;
  27|                       f. Encourage the development of mixed use buildings and campuses that are designed and constructed in a manner that is
  28|                       contextually sensitive to the existing structures and facilities.
  29|                       4.17.2. Establishment
  30|                       The Village Center District is hereby established as of 1 January 2016 and consists of the area shown as the Village Center
  31|                       District on Town of Lunenburg Zoning Map on file with the Town/City Clerk and dated 2 May 2015 as may be amended
  32|                       from time to time by Town Meeting.
  33|                       4.17.3. Definitions
  34|                       Artist Space: A shop for the creation and/or sale of goods made by a potter, ceramicist, silversmith, jewelry maker, painter,
  35|                       photographer or other fine artist. This space may also serve as a living space for the artist provided there is adequate
  36|                       separation between uses per the governing Building and Health Codes.
  37|                       Banner: A strip of cloth or other man made fabric on which a sign is painted, silk-screened or printed. The display area shall
  38|                       be defined as the area of one face of the banner. The banner shall not exceed (40) square feet and shall not be displayed for
  39|                       more than fourteen (14) consecutive days.
  40|                       Bed & Breakfast: Bed and Breakfast, or Bed and Breakfast Establishment provided that:
  41|                       a) The dwelling is owner occupied.

  33|                        ARTICLE 39. To see if the Town will vote to authorize the enactment of a bylaw regulating the use of vehicles
  34|                        on Whalom Lake.
  35|                        Table of Contents
  36|                        Section 1. Purpose and Scope
  37|                       Section 2. Definitions
  38|                       Section 3. Operation of Snow Vehicles and All-Terrain Vehicles
  39|                       Section 4. Operation of Motor Vehicles prohibited
  40|                       Section 5. Public Access Only
  41|                        Section 6. Penalties
  42|                        Section 1. Purpose and Scope
  43|                       The Purpose and scope of this bylaw is to protect the safety of the public to prevent the destruction of aquatic life,
  44|                       waterfowl and other wildlife, the decay of water quality and damage to abutting private and public lands by the
  45|                       inappropriate use of motor vehicles, recreation vehicles or snow vehicles on the waters or frozen waters of Whalom
  46|                       Lake; to promote voluntary compliance with all applicable laws relating to the operation of motor vehicles and when
  47|                       necessary to deter noncompliance through fines and penalties.
  48|                        Section 2. Definitions
  49|                                   a) Motor Vehicle: any motor vehicle as defined in M.G.L. Chapter 90, § 1.
  50|                                                                                                    168

===PAGE 169=== (ocr, 47 lines)
   1|                                    a) All-terrain vehicle: means a motorized recreational vehicle designed or modified for travel on three or
   2|                                          four low pressure tires and having a seat designed to be straddled by the operator and handlebars for
   3|                                         steering control, and recreational vehicle or off-highway vehicle as defined in CMA 323, § 3.02 and
   4|                                          governed by M.G.L.Chapter 90B.
   5|                                    b) Snow vehicle: a motor vehicle designed to travel over ice or snow, having a curb weight of not more
   6|                                          than 453 kilograms or 21000 pounds, driven by track or tracks in contact with the snow or ice and
   7|                                          steered by a ski or skis in contact with the snow or ice as defined in CMA 323, § 302 and governed by
   8|                                         M.G.L. Chapter 90B.
   9|                                    c) Operation: (1) to ride in or on and control the operation of, or to maintain, suffer, supervise, or permit
  10|                                          the operation of, or to push a snow vehicle or a recreational vehicle, or, (2) In the case of a motor
  11|                                          vehicle, any person who makes use of any mechanical or electrical agency, which alone or in sequence
  12|                                          will set in motion the motive power of the vehicle, whether or not the engine is not running; or (3) any
  13|                                          person who utilizes any combination of actions that would set the vehicle in motion.
  14|                                    d) Public Access: shall mean the public access located in the City of Leominster or any other place where
  15|                                          Whalom Lake can be accessed by the public.
  16|                                    e) Law Enforcement Officer: any police officer, constable or other officer authorized to make arrests or
  17|                                          serve process provided hi is in uniform or displays his/her bade of office.
  18|                                    f) Board: Town of Lunenburg, Board of Selectmen
  19|                       Section 3. Operation of Snow Vehicles and All-Terrain Vehicles
  20|                                    A. No person, or group of persons shall operate, or cause to be operated on the waters or frozen waters of
  21|                                         Whalom Lake, any snow vehicles that are not in compliance with Massachusetts CMR 323 § 2.01 to
  22|                                         3.09 & MGL c. 90 § 21 to 35.
  23|                                    B. When the Town of Lunenburg or any other agency or state agency duly authorized by law has posted
  24|                                         the waters or frozen waters of Whalom Lake to prohibit access for or use of snow vehicles or all-
  25|                                         terrain vehicles, no person, or group of persons shall operate any snow vehicle or all-terrain vehicle
  26|                                          upon such waters or frozen waters. In the absence of such a posting, persons utilizing water or the
  27|                                          frozen water of Whalom Lake do so at their own risk and the Town of Lunenburg assumes no
  28|                                         responsibility either implied or expressed for the safety of any person who voluntarily assumes a
  29|                                          known and obvious risk inherent in such activities. No person shall operate a snow vehicle or all-
  30|                                         terrain vehicle upon any frozen waters of Whalom Lake under any circumstance unless a minimum of
  31|                                         five inches of solid ice cover is present. The operator shall determine the thickness of the ice, and
  32|                                          assumes all responsibility in undertaking an activity with an inherent and known risk.
  33|                        Section 4. Operation of Motor Vehicles Prohibited
  34|                                    A. No person, group of persons or organizations shall operate, or cause to be operated, any motor vehicle,
  35|                                          as defined in MGL c. 90 § 1 on the waters or frozen waters of Whalom Lake.
  36|                       Section 5. Public Access Only
  37|                                   B. No Snow Vehicle or All-terrain vehicle shall enter upon Whalom Lake except by public access or by
  38|                                         written permission by the landowner.
  39|                        Section 6. Penalties
  40|                       This bylaw may be enforced through any lawful means in law or in equity including, but not limited, to,
  41|                       enforcement by criminal complaint or fines pursuant to G.L. D.40 § 21D, by the Board of Selectman, the Town
  42|                       Manager or their duly authorized agents, or any police officer. Whether enforced through criminal or civil process,
  43|                       the fine for a violation of this bylaw shall be three hundred dollars ($300.) for each offense. Board of Selectmen to
  44|                       make recommendation at ATM, Finance Committee reports no direct financial impact.
