  48|                        Amendments
  49|                        Article I. Buyers and Sellers of Goods and Electronics
  50|                        Section I. Licensing Authority and Requirements
  51|                        Subsection A.
  52|                        The Board of Selectmen may license suitable persons to be pawnbrokers or buyers of goods pursuant to law.
  53|                       Licenses shall expire on the last day of December annually no matter when obtained during the preceding year. Such
  54|                       licenses shall not be valid to protect the holders thereof in a building or place other than that designated in the
  55|                                                                                                    170

===PAGE 171=== (ocr, 54 lines)
   1|                       license, unless consent to removal is granted by the Board of Selectmen. Applications for new licenses under the
   2|                       rule may be filed at any time with the Board of Selectmen. Applications for the reissue of licenses already existing
   3|                        should be filed at least 30 days before the expiration of such licenses. Persons whose licenses have expired and have
   4|                       not been reissued will be liable to prosecution if carrying on business for which the license is required. Every person
   5|                       so licensed shall, at the time of receiving such license, file a bond as provided by M.G.L. c. 140 § 77 as amended.
   6|                        Subsection B.
   7|                        Persons who engage in or carry on the business of lending money on mortgages, deposits or pledges of wearing
   8|                       apparel, jewelry, ornaments, household goods or other personal property, or of purchasing such property on
   9|                        condition of selling the same back again at a stipulated price, when the property so mortgaged, pledged or purchased
  10|                       is deposited with the lender, must be licensed as pawnbrokers. This provision, however, does not apply to loans
  11|                        made on stocks, bonds, notes or other written or printed evidence of ownership of property or of indebtedness to the
  12|                       holder or owner of such securities. (M.G.L. c. 140, § 70 - 85)
  13|                        Section II. Interest Rates
  14|                              A. Licensed pawnbrokers may charge interest at the rate of 3% per month, and in no event may they charge
  15|                                    more than the rate allowed by the Massachusetts Commissioner of Banks.
  16|                              B. No such pawnbrokers shall charge or receive any greater rate of interest, and interest shall be determined
  17|                                    on the precise sum advanced by the lender.
  18|                              C. No pawnbroker shall make or receive any extra charge or fee for storage, care or safekeeping of any goods,
  19|                                   articles or things pawned with him. (M.G.L. c. 140, 8 78)
  20|                              D.
  21|                        Section III. Police may enter and inspect premises and records
  22|                        Any officer of the Lunenburg Police may at any time enter upon any premises used by a licensed pawnbroker or
  23|                        buyer for the purposes of his or her business, ascertain how he or she conducts his or her business and examine all
  24|                       articles taken in pawn or bought, or kept or stored in or upon said premises and all books and inventories shall be
  25|                        exhibited to any above name whenever a demand shall be made for such exhibition. (M.G.L. c. 140, 874) (Penalty
  26|                       for refusal, M.G.L. c. 140, 874)
  27|                        Section IV. Numbering of pawned articles
  28|                        Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall at the time of making any loan, attach a number to the article taken in
  29|                       pawn or bought and shall make entry of such number in the book provided for in Section V. of this article. Section
  30|                        V. Maintenance of records; contents; photo identification
  31|                               A. Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall keep a book of style and size in which shall be legibly written in
  32|                                     ink in the English language at the time of making each loan, an account and description, including all
  33|                                     distinguishing marks and numbers and serial numbers of the goods, articles or things pledged or pawned,
  34|                                     the amount of money loaned or paid thereon, the day and hour when it was pawned, the rate of interest to
  35|                                     be paid on such loan and the number of such article as same. No entry made in said book shall be erased,
  36|                                     obliterated or defaced. Electronic record keeping by the pawnbroker or buyer is acceptable as long as the
  37|                                     records meet all the bylaw requirements.
  38|                               B. Every pawnbroker or buyer shall photograph any person pawning or pledging articles and keep such
  39|                                     photographs with said books as part of his or her records. (M.G.L. c. 140, § 79).
  40|                               C. For all transactions, every pawnbroker or buyer shall also require positive identification and shall record
  41|                                     the type of identification presented and record the date of birth from any person pawning, pledging or
  42|                                     selling any article. Positive identification shall mean any picture identification card issued by a
  43|                               D.
  44|                        Section VI. Pledge cards; contents; retention
  45|                        Each pledger shall be required by the pawnbroker to sign his/her name and age and address on a card. In the event
  46|                       that the pledger is unable to write, the pawnbroker shall fill in the name, age and address on such card, together with
  47|                       a notation stating that the pledger was unable to do so. Such card shall be retained seven years in an alphabetical
  48|                       index file by the licensed pawnbrokers.
  49|                       Section VII. Copy of required record to pledger
  50|                        Every pawnbroker or buyer shall at the time of making such loan deliver to the person who pawns or pledges any
  51|                       goods, articles or things, a memorandum or note signed by him, containing the substance of the entry required to be
  52|                       made in his book by the provisions of Section V. and no charge shall be made or required by any pawnbroker or
  53|                       buyer for any such entry, memorandum or note. (M.G.L. c. 140, § 80)
  54|                                                                                                    171

===PAGE 172=== (ocr, 55 lines)
   1|                        Section VIII. Daily report to police
   2|                           Subsection A. Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall make out and deliver a report of transactions to the
   3|                        Lunenburg Police Chief or his designee every day before the hour of 10:00 a.m., a legible and correct list containing
   4|                       an accurate description, including all distinguishable marks, numbers and serial numbers of all articles taken in
   5|                        pawn or bought during the preceding business day, the respective numbers of such articles as provided by Section
   6|                       IV of this bylaw, the amount loaned or paid thereon and the time when such articles were pawned or bought. This
   7|                       report can be done electronically, via the Internet, or faxed to the Lunenburg Police Chief or his designee. If during
   8|                       the preceding day no articles have been taken in by such pawnbroker or buyer, he or she is required to report
   9|                       affirmatively. This report can be done both electronically via the Internet and by fax.
  10|                          Subsection B. If any goods or articles pawned or pledged and in the possession of a pawnbroker or buyer are
  11|                       subsequently determined to be stolen property by a member of the Lunenburg Police Department or the
  12|                       Massachusetts State Police, or if the rightful owner identifies property in the possession of a pawnbroker or buyer
  13|                       and the property so identified is confirmed to be stolen goods by a member of the Lunenburg Police Department or
  14|                       Massachusetts State Police, said property shall be returned to the rightful owner at no cost to such owner.
  15|                        Section IX. Posting Requirements
  16|                          Subsection A. Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall post in a conspicuous place in his or her shop or office a
  17|                       copy of the statutes, ordinances and police regulations relating to pawnbrokers/buyers, to be furnished by the
  18|                        Lunenburg Police Department's Police Chief or designee, and shall put in some suitable and conspicuous place in
  19|                       his shop a sign having his/her name and occupation legibly inscribed thereon in large lettering.
  20|                          Subsection B. No pawnbroker or buyer shall place or maintain any signs or devices upon or in connection with his
  21|                        or her licensed premises indicating or tending to indicate that any form of business is conducted therein which he or
  22|                        she is not legally authorized to pursue.
  23|                        Section X. Hours of Operation
  24|                        Pawnbroker or buyer may have his/her shop open for transactions between sunrise and 10:00 p.m. in the evening of
  25|                       any weekday and weekend. Under no circumstances can a pawnbroker or buyer operate after the hour of 10:00 p.m.
  26|                        Section XI. Disposition of pledged articles
  27|                          Subsection A. Articles deposited in pawn with a licensed pawnbroker shall unless redeemed, be retained by
  28|                       him/her on the premises occupied by him/her for their business for at least four months after the date of deposit.
  29|                       apply the proceeds thereof in satisfaction of the debt or demand and the expense of the notice and sale and pay any
  30|                       surplus to the person entitled thereto on demand.
  31|                          Subsection C. No such sale of any article which is not of a perishable nature shall be made unless not less than 10
  32|                        days prior to the sale a written notice of the intended sale shall have been sent by registered mail to the person
  33|                        entitled to the payment of any surplus as aforesaid, addressed to his residence as appearing in the records of such
  34|                       pawnbrokers. Proof of registered mail shall be kept on file for one year after the date of sale.
  35|                          Subsection D. No article taken in pawn by such pawnbroker or buyer shall be disposed of otherwise than as above
  36|                        provided, any agreement or contract between the parties thereto to the contrary notwithstanding.
  37|                          Subsection E. Articles of personal apparel shall not be deemed to be of a perishable nature within the meaning of
  38|                       this section. (M.G.L. c. 140, § 71)
  39|                       Section XII. Prohibitions
  40|                          Subsection A. No pawnbroker or buyer shall make a loan, directly or indirectly, to a person under the age of 18,
  41|                        knowing or having reason to believe him or her to be such.
  42|                          Subsection B. No pawnbroker or buyer shall loan money secured by deposit or pledge of a firearm, rifle, shotgun
  43|                        or machine gun. (M.G.L. c. 140, § 131B)
  44|                          Subsection C. No pawnbroker or buyer shall hold a license to sell, rent, or lease a firearm, rifle, shotgun, or
  45|                       machine gun.
  46|                       Section XIII. Complaints, Disciplinary Action; Hearing
  47|                          Subsection A. Complaints concerning licensed pawnbrokers or buyers shall be investigated by the Lunenburg
  48|                        Police Department under the direction of the Chief of Police. The Chief of Police or his designee will provide a
  49|                        disciplinary request to the Board of Selectmen for actionable complaints lodged against licensees.
  50|                          Subsection B. In the event the Chief of Police determines that disciplinary action should be instituted against a
  51|                       licensed pawnbroker or buyer, the Chief of Police shall cause to be served upon the licensed pawnbroker or buyer
  52|                       notice as to the time, date and place of hearing and of the charge with a statement of the reasons for the proposed
  53|                        disciplinary action. Hearings shall be conducted in accordance with law.
  54|                        Section XIV. Suspension or Revocation of License
  55|                                                                                                    172

===PAGE 173=== (ocr, 56 lines)
   1|                        The Board of Selectmen may suspend or revoke licenses provided for by this article for any cause which the Board
   2|                        of Selectmen deems sufficient. Offenses which may result in the suspension or revocation of a pawnbroker's or
   3|                       buyer's license include but are not limited to the following:
   4|                       a) A violation of any section of this article.
   5|                       b) A violation of any provision of any statute or applicable law.
   6|                        Article II. Sale, Exchange or Purchase of Metals
   7|                        Section I. Findings
   8|                        The Town of Lunenburg finds that there is a cognizable risk for stolen metals to end up in the possession of even
   9|                       legitimate businesses which trade in metals, including precious metals. Certain criminals bring stolen metals,
  10|                       including precious metals to dealers in jewelry and scrap metal. The victims of theft have only small hope of
  11|                       recovering their property unless the people and entities who receive scrap metals and jewelry are regulated in a
  12|                       manner which identifies both the metal received by the dealers and the persons who deliver the metal to these
  13|                        dealers. There is an Internet alert system used by the Lunenburg Police Department which reports stolen metals.
  14|                        Monitoring transactions within the town and identifying both the metals and the persons selling or delivering these
  15|                        metals will serve both to deter theft and to enable the Lunenburg Police Department to trace and recover stolen
  16|                        property and return it to the rightful owners.
  17|                        Section II. Definitions
  18|                       As used in Article II, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:
  19|                       ARTICLE: Any metal which is subject to Article II and is exchanged, sold, collected, bartered or received by a
  20|                       person dealing in metals.
  21|                        CHIEF OF POLICE: The Chief of the Lunenburg Police Department or his designee.
  22|                       EXCHANGE: Receiving, purchasing, selling or bartering metals, including precious metals and industrial scrap
  23|                       metals.
  24|                       METAL: A chemical element that is malleable, opaque and ductile, usually solid, which has a characteristic luster,
  25|                       is a good conductor of heat and electricity, and can be melted or fused, hammered into thin sheets, or drawn into
  26|                        wires, e.g., copper, aluminum, gold, silver or iron or other metals.
  27|                        PRECIOUS METAL(S): Any metal which is considered valuable, such as silver, gold, platinum and copper
  28|                        without regard to the form or amount of such precious metal.
  29|                        BOARD: Board of Selectmen
  30|                        Section III. License Required
  31|                       a) No person shall collect, deal in, exchange, buy, or keep a shop or place for the exchange, purchase, sale or barter
  32|                       of metals, including precious metals and industrial metals, in any building or place within the limits of the town
  33|                        without having a license issued by the Board of Selectman. The license requirement and the other requirements of
  34|                       this Article II shall not apply to commercial haulers having valid, current United States Department of
  35|                        Transportation stickers affixed to their vehicles.
  36|                       b) Board of Selectmen may for a fee set by said board and based upon an application devised by said board, license
  37|                        suitable persons to be dealers in and keepers of shops or locations for the purchase, sale or barter of precious metals
  38|                        at such places within the town as may be designated in such license. The Board of Selectmen may place reasonable
  39|                       conditions on such licenses which shall be inscribed on the face of the license. A license shall be limited to a
  40|                       specific address stated thereon. Subject to the notice and appeal provisions contained in Section IX (E), (2), (3) of
  41|                       this Article II, the Board of Selectmen may deny a license to any person who in the exercise of his reasonable
  42|                       discretion is unsuitable.
  43|                       c) All metal dealer licenses shall expire annually on the last day in December. The license holders shall be
  44|                       responsible for submitting an application for license renewal with the license fee to the Board of Selectmen at least
  45|                        30 days prior to the last day in December. Upon receipt of an application for renewal, the Board shall consider the
  46|                       performance of the licensee during the previous year and shall determine whether the licensee had been found in
  47|                        violation of this Article II and other ordinances and regulations of the town applicable to metal dealers.
  48|                       d) The Board of Selectmen may promulgate reasonable regulations not inconsistent with this Article II which shall
  49|                       be binding upon all licensees. No regulation shall take effect until the expiration of 30 days from the date the
  50|                       regulation(s) is delivered or mailed to the person(s) then licensed. The Board of Selectmen shall deliver a complete
  51|                       set of regulations and any amendments thereto to the Town Clerk. The Town Clerk shall maintain the complete set
  52|                        of all regulations in a book available to the public.
  53|                       e) The obligation to obtain a license as required by this section will take effect 45 days after it is finally enacted.
  54|                        Section IV. Transactions with Minors
  55|                        No licensee shall, directly or indirectly, exchange any metals with a person under the age of 18.
  56|                                                                                                    173

===PAGE 174=== (ocr, 54 lines)
   1|                        Section V. Waiting Period
   2|                        No article exchanged, purchased or received shall be sold, or altered in appearance, form or substance until a period
   3|                       of at least twenty-one (21) days have elapsed from the date of its purchase or receipt. All articles exchanged,
   4|                       purchased or received must be made available to the Lunenburg Police Department upon request within 24 hours of
   5|                       such request, and the Police Department may investigate to determine if any article is or may be stolen property.
   6|                        This waiting period does not apply to scrap metal yards which are exempt from any waiting period.
   7|                        Section VI. Daily Report
   8|                        Every licensee shall electronically create and send to the Police Chief or his designee on a form, in the manner and
   9|                       at the time prescribed by the Police Chief or his designee, a legible complete list containing an accurate description
  10|                       of all metal articles received by the licensee during the previous 24 hours. The description must include: the type of
  11|                       metal, the size and/or quantity, whether the article is or may be a precious metal, if applicable; whether the article is
  12|                       typically used by or associated with a male or female, the wording of any engraving, whether the article has any
  13|                       gems or precious stones, any identifying number and every other identifiable trait.
  14|                        Section VII. Recordkeeping Requirements
  15|                        A. Every licensee shall, at the time of making any exchange or receipt of any article, assign and attach a number to
  16|                       each article received and shall make entry of such number in the book described in Subsection B.
  17|                        B. Every licensee shall keep a book in which shall be legibly written in ink, in the English language, at the time the
  18|                       licensee receives any article, the following information:
  19|                       1) An account and description, including all distinguishing or identifying marks and numbers of every article
  20|                       received by the licensee.
  21|                       2) The amount of money, if any, paid for the article.
  22|                       3) The date and hour when it was received.
  23|                       4) The name, age, permanent address and telephone number of the person from who purchased or received.
  24|                        5) A copy of the document used to identify the person giving the article to the licensee.
  25|                        C. Every licensee shall require positive identification from any person selling or exchanging any article. The
  26|                       licensee shall copy and record the type of identification presented and the date of birth from any person giving or
  27|                       exchanging any article. Positive identification means only a government-issued document with the person's name
  28|                                             eth ile bok Feared by is eins bal be mad, blemied or dece in any manor
  29|                        whatsoever. The book shall at all times be open for the inspection by the Police Chief or any police officer. The
  30|                       licensee shall keep and maintain all the records required by this Article II for a period of three years from the date of
  31|                       the last entry in any book.
  32|                        Section VIII. Posting of Name, Occupation and License; Inspections
  33|                        Every licensee shall post in some suitable and conspicuous place where he or she receives or exchanges articles, a
  34|                       sign having his/ her full legal name, and his/her business name, if different, and his/her occupation legibly described
  35|                       thereon in large letters. The current license shall also be so posted. The location where transactions occur, the store
  36|                       or shop and all articles exchanged and or kept therein or received therein and the book and documents required by
  37|                       this Article II, may at all times be examined by the Police Chief or any police officer at their request.
  38|                       Section IX. Violations and Penalties
  39|                        A. Whoever not having a valid license as required by this Article II, exchanges, collects, deals in or barters metals in
  40|                       any place or manner other than that designated in his license, or after notice to him that his license has been revoked,
  41|                        or whoever violates this Article II or any rule, regulation or restriction contained in his license, or any regulation
  42|                       promulgated by the Town of Lunenburg shall be subject to the fines and sanctions described in this section. Each
  43|                        day of such violation shall constitute a separate offense.
  44|                        B. The fine for breach of the duty imposed by this Article II is three hundred dollars ($300). Each day on which the
  45|                       person continues in violation shall be considered as a separate violation.
  46|                        C. This Article II may at the discretion of the Chief of Police be enforced by civil process or by noncriminal
  47|                        disposition as provided in M.G.L. c. 40, 8 21D. The Chief of Police or any Lunenburg police officer may issue
  48|                       tickets to enforce this Article II. If enforced civilly by ticket each day on which a violation exists shall be deemed to
  49|                        be a separate offense and the violator shall be subject to the following fines:
  50|                              1) First violation: $150.
  51|                              2) Second violation: $200.
  52|                             3) Third violation: $300.
  53|                              4) Fourth and each subsequent violation: $300.
  54|                                                                                                    174

===PAGE 175=== (ocr, 55 lines)
   1|                        D. In addition to the penalties set forth above, the enforcing authority may seek an injunction from an appropriate
   2|                        court to restrain any violation of this Article II, any regulation promulgated by the Town of Lunenburg or any
   3|                        condition inscribed on a license.
   4|                        E. The Board of Selectmen may terminate any license or refuse to renew any license for violation of this Article II, a
   5|                        regulation promulgated by the Town of Lunenburg or any condition inscribed on the license. The Board of
   6|                        Selectmen shall use the procedure described in this section.
   7|                            1) Notice of violation. Whenever it comes to the attention of the Board of Selectmen that a violation of this
   8|                        Article II, a regulation promulgated by the Town of Lunenburg or a condition inscribed on a license, the Board shall
   9|                        by written notice, deliver personally or send by certified mail to the licensee notifying him of the violation and order
  10|                        the person to cease and desist. Depending on the severity of the violation as determined by him, the Board of
  11|                        Selectmen may terminate the license. The Board shall also provide notice described herein if it denies an application
  12|                        for a license stating the reasons therefor.
  13|                             2) Contents of notice. The written notice to the licensee shall contain a description of the violation(s) and the
  14|                        date(s) of occurrence and a citation to the section of the ordinance, regulation or license condition which the licensee
  15|                        is alleged to have violated. The notice will, if applicable, describe what the licensee must do to comply, whether the
  16|                        Board of Selectmen intends to terminate the license and the effective date of the termination which shall afford the
  17|                        licensee at least seven days to file an appeal of the proposed termination with the Board. In the case of denial of a
  18|                        license, the notice shall state the reasons for the denial.
  19|                            3) Appeal. Upon receipt of a notice of license termination, or denial, the licensee may, within seven days of'
  20|                       receipt of the notice, file a written appeal by delivery or certified mail to the Board of Selectmen's office during the
  21|                       hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on days when Town Hall is open for business. When the Board of Selectmen
  22|                       receives an appeal, they shall appoint a neutral hearing officer who will take testimony from any persons with
  23|                       knowledge of the facts including any police officer and the appellant. The appellant may be represented by counsel
  24|                        and any person so testifying will be subject to cross examination. The proceedings will be governed by the rules of
  25|                        evidence applicable to an informal administrative hearing. The hearing officer will assure that an appropriate record,
  26|                       including any documents submitted, is made and kept. The decision of the hearing officer will be written and final.
  27|                        F. The Board of Selectmen, subject to the process described in this section, may refuse to renew any license. The
  28|                        Board shall not issue a license to any person convicted of a felony.

  36|                        ARTICLE 42. To see if the Town will vote to enact a bylaw to restrict Sexual Offender Residency and create
  37|                        Sex Offender Safety Zones
  38|                        Table of Contents
  39|                        Section 1 Findings and Intent
  40|                        Section 2 Definitions
  41|                        Section 3 Sex Offender Residence Prohibition
  42|                        Section 4 Evidentiary Matters; Measurements
  43|                        Section 5 Notice to Move
  44|                        Section 6 Exceptions
  45|                        Section 7 Forfeiture of Exception
  46|                        Section 8 Penalties
  47|                        Section 9 Safety Zone
  48|                        Section 10 Maps and List of Safety Zones
  49|                        Section 11 Severability
  50|                        Section 1. Findings and Intent
  51|                              A.        It is the intent of this bylaw to serve and to protect the Town's compelling interest to promote, protect
  52|                                        and improve the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town by creating areas around
  53|                                        locations where children, or the elderly regularly congregate in concentrated numbers wherein certain
  54|                                         sex offenders are prohibited from loitering and establishing temporary or permanent residence.
  55|                                                                                                    175

===PAGE 176=== (ocr, 59 lines)
   1|                              A. After careful consideration, the Town finds that this bylaw is the most narrowly tailored means of
   2|                                        limiting, to the fullest extent possible, the opportunity for certain sex offenders to approach or otherwise
   3|                                        come in contact with children or the elderly in places where children or the elderly would naturally
   4|                                        congregate, and that the protection of the health and safety of our children and elderly is a compelling
   5|                                        governmental interest.
   6|                              B.        By the enactment of this or any other bylaw, the Town understands that it cannot remove the threat
   7|                                        posed to or guarantee the safety of children or the elderly or assure the public that sex offenders will
   8|                                        comply with the mandates of this bylaw. This legislation is intended to create a civil, non-punitive
   9|                                        regulatory scheme in order to protect children and the elderly to the extent possible under the
  10|                                        circumstances and not as a punitive measure of any kind.
  11|                              C.         Certain sex offenders pose a clear threat to the children and the elderly residing or visiting in the
  12|                                        community. Because certain sex offenders are more likely than any other type of offender to reoffend by
  13|                                        another sexual offense, the Town desires to impose safety precautions in furtherance of the goal of'
  14|                                        protecting the children and elderly. The purpose of this bylaw is to reduce the potential risk of harm to
  15|                                        children and the elderly in the community by limiting the ability of certain classified levels of sex
  16|                                        offenders to be in contact with unsuspecting children and the elderly in locations that are primarily
  17|                                        designed for use by or are primarily used by children and the elderly, the grounds of a public or private
  18|                                        school for children, a center of facility that provides day care or children's services, a park, other public
  19|                                        recreational facility, elderly housing facilities or the Senior Citizen's Center. The Town desires to add
  20|                                        location restrictions to such offenders to the extent state law is silent.
  21|                       Section 2. Definitions
  22|                              1) "Camp Bus Stop" Any area designated by a private/public youth camp as a camp bus stop which has been
  23|                                    designated in a list maintained by the Town and available to the public.
  24|                              2) "Day Care Center" means an establishment, whether public or private, which provides care for children and
  25|                                    is registered with and licensed pursuant to the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts by the
  26|                                    Department of Early Education and Care.
  27|                             3)   "Elder" or "Elderly" means a person or persons over 60 years of age. "Elderly Housing Facility" or "Senior
  28|                                    Citizens Center" or "Over 55 Community" means any building or buildings which provide a group
  29|                                    residence for the elderly or a location where the elderly gather and/or reside that is located within the Town
  30|                                    of Lunenburg, Massachusetts.
  31|                                  "Establishing a Residence" means to set up or bring into being a dwelling place or an abode where a person
  32|                                    sleeps, which may include more than one location, and may be mobile or transitory, or by means of
  33|                                    purchasing real property or entering into a lease or rental agreement for real property.
  34|                             5)  "Loitering" means to remain for more than fifteen (15) minutes within a five hundred (500) foot distance
  35|                                    of the location in question.
  36|                                   "Park" means active and passive public land designated for recreational or athletic use by the Town of
  37|                                    Lunenburg, Massachusetts and located within the Town of Lunenburg Massachusetts.
  38|                             7)    "Permanent Residence" means a place where a person lives, abides, lodges, or resides for five (5) or more
  39|                                    consecutive days or fourteen (14) or more days in the aggregate during any calendar year.
  40|                                   "Recreational Facility" means a playground, a forest preserve, conservation area, jogging trail or running
  41|                                    track, hiking or biking trail, beach, water park, swimming pool, wading pool, soccer field, baseball field,
  42|                                   football field, basketball court or hockey rink, whether publicly or privately owned, to which the public has
  43|                                   a right of access as an invitee and which is located within the Town of Lunenburg, Massachusetts.
  44|                              9) "School" means any public or private educational facility that provides services to children in grades
  45|                                    Kindergarten - 12, or any one or more of such grades.
  46|                              10) "School Bus Stop" means any area designated by the public school district or by a private or parochial
  47|                                    school within the Town of Lunenburg, Massachusetts as a school bus stop, which school bus stop has been
  48|                                    designated in a list maintained by the Town and available to the public.
  49|                              11) "Sex Offender" and "Sex offense" shall have the same meaning for purposes of this bylaw as provided for
  50|                                   in G.L. c. 6, $ 178C.
  51|                              12) "Sex Offense Involving a Child" shall have the same meaning for purposes of this bylaw as provided for in
  52|                                    G.L. c. 6, § 178C.
  53|                              13) "Temporary Residence" means a place where a person lives, abides, lodges or resides for a period of less
  54|                                    than five (5) consecutive days or fourteen (14) days in the aggregate during any calendar year.
  55|                        Section 3. Sex Offender Residence Prohibition
  56|                       It is unlawful for any sex offender who has been finally classified as a Level 2 or 3 offender pursuant to the
  57|                        guidelines of the Sex Offender Registry Board, for as long as so classified, to establish a permanent residence or
  58|                       temporary residence in the Town of Lunenburg, Massachusetts within one thousand (1,000) feet of the property on
  59|                                                                                                    176

===PAGE 177=== (ocr, 59 lines)
   1|                       which any public or private school, park, playground, beach, biking/hiking trail, other recreational facility, elderly
   2|                       housing facility, over 55 community, senior citizens center, or licensed day-care center is located.
   3|                        Section 4. Evidentiary Matters; Measurements
   4|                        For purposes of determining the minimum distance requirement, the separation shall be measured by following a
   5|                       straight line from the outer property line of the permanent residence to the nearest outer property line of any public
   6|                       or private school, park, playground, beach, biking/hiking trail, other recreational facility, elderly housing facility,
   7|                       over 55 community, senior citizens center, or licensed day-care center.
   8|                        Section 5. Notice to Move
   9|                        Any sex offender who has been finally classified as a Level 2 or 3 offender pursuant to the guidelines of the Sex
  10|                        Offender Registry Board, for as long as so classified, who establishes a permanent residence or temporary residence
  11|                       in the Town of Lunenburg, Massachusetts within one thousand (1,000) feet of any public or private school, park,
  12|                       playground, beach, biking/hiking trail, other recreational facility, elderly housing facility, over 55 community, senior
  13|                       citizens center, or licensed day-care center shall be in violation of this bylaw and shall, within thirty (30) days of
  14|                       receipt of written notice of the sex offender's noncompliance with this bylaw, move from said location to a new
  15|                       location, but said location may not be within one thousand (1,000) feet of any public or private school, park,
  16|                       playground, beach, biking/hiking trail, other recreational facility, elderly housing facility, over 55 community, senior
  17|                       citizens center, or licensed day-care center within the Town of Lunenburg, Massachusetts. Furthermore it shall be a
  18|                       separate violation each day that a sex offender shall move from one location in the Town of Lunenburg to another
  19|                       that is within one thousand (1,000) feet of any public or private school, park, playground, beach, biking/hiking trail,
  20|                       other recreational facility, elderly housing facility, over 55 community, senior citizens center, or licensed day-care
  21|                        Section 6. Exceptions
  22|                        A sex offender residing within 1,000 feet of any public or private school, park, playground, beach, biking/hiking
  23|                       trail, other recreational facility, elderly housing facility, over 55 communities, senior citizens center, or licensed day-
  24|                       care center does not commit a violation of this bylaw if any of the following apply:
  25|                                1)     The person established the permanent residence and reported and registered the residence, as required by
  26|                                       the Sex Offender Registry Law and any applicable regulations of the Massachusetts Sex Offender
  27|                                       Registry Board, prior to the effective date of this bylaw, and:
  28|                                 a)     Permanent residence was established by purchasing the real property where the residence is established,
  29|                                        as long as the registered sex offender continues to reside in and does not move to another restricted
  30|                                        location in Lunenburg different from the permanent residence established prior to the effective date of
  31|                                       this bylaw;
  32|                                 b)     Permanent residence was established through a valid, fixed-term, written and/or oral lease or rental
  33|                                        agreement, executed prior to the effective date of this bylaw, as long as the registered sex offender
  34|                                        continues to reside within and does not move to another restricted location in Lunenburg different from
  35|                                        the permanent residence established prior to the effective date of this bylaw; or
  36|                                 c)     Permanent residence was established through a written and/or oral lease or rental agreement at the will
  37|                                        of the landlord, as long as the registered sex offender continues to reside within and does not move to
  38|                                        another restricted location in Lunenburg different from the permanent residence established prior to the
  39|                                        effective date of this bylaw.
  40|                                  2) The person was a minor when the relevant crime was committed and was not convicted as an adult.
  41|                                  3) The person is a minor.
  42|                                   4) The public or private school, park, playground, beach, biking/hiking trail, other recreational facility,
  43|                                    elderly housing facility, over 55 community, senior citizens center, or licensed day-care center was
  44|                                    established after such person established the permanent residence and reported and registered the residence
  45|                                    pursuant to the Sex Offender Registry Law and any applicable regulations of the Massachusetts Sex
  46|                                    Offender Registry Board.
  47|                                    5) The person is required to serve a sentence at a jail, prison, juvenile facility, or other correctional
  48|                                    institution or facility located within the aforementioned 1,000 foot area.
  49|                                    6) The person is admitted to and/or subject to an order of commitment at a public or private facility for the
  50|                                    care and treatment of mentally ill persons pursuant to G.L. c. 123 located within the aforementioned 1,000
  51|                                    foot area.
  52|                                    7) The person is a mentally ill person subject to guardianship pursuant to order or supervision of the
  53|                                    Probate and Family Court or a mentally retarded person subject to guardianship pursuant to G.L. c. 201
  54|                                    §6A, residing with his or her guardian or residing within a group residence that is professionally staffed and
  55|                                    supervised 24 hours a day and located within the aforementioned 1,000 foot area.
  56|                        Section 7. Forfeiture of Exception
  57|                       If, either after the effective date of this bylaw or after a new public or private school, park, playground, beach,
  58|                        biking/hiking trail, other recreational facility, elderly housing facility, over 55 community, senior
  59|                                                                                                    177

===PAGE 178=== (ocr, 57 lines)
   1|                                    citizens center, or licensed day-care center opens, an indictment or conviction of another sex offense is
   2|                                   issued by a court against a Level 2 or 3 Sex Offender otherwise enjoying an exception under this bylaw, he
   3|                                    or she shall immediately forfeit that exception and be required to comply with this bylaw.
   4|                        Section 8. Penalties
   5|                                  1) Criminal Complaint. Violation of the residency provisions of this bylaw may be enforced by criminal
   6|                                         complaint filed by any police officer of the Town of Lunenburg, Massachusetts. Each day a violation
   7|                                         exists shall constitute a separate violation. The fine for each violation upon conviction shall be three
   8|                                        hundred dollars ($300).
   9|                                   2) Noncriminal Disposition. In addition to enforcement by criminal complaint, violation of the residency
  10|                                         provisions of this bylaw may be enforced through any lawful means in law or in equity by any police
  11|                                        officer of the Town of Lunenburg including, but not limited to, enforcement by non-criminal
  12|                                         disposition pursuant to G.L. c. 40, § 21D. Each day a violation exists shall constitute a separate
  13|                                         violation. The penalties for noncriminal disposition shall be as follows:
  14|                                                 a) First offense: Notification to offender that he/she has thirty (30) days to move.
  15|                                                 b) Subsequent offense: noncriminal fine of three hundred dollars ($300), enforceable by a
  16|                                                       police officer, and written notification to the property owner, if other than the offender, the
  17|                                                       offender's landlord, parole officer and/or probation officer, and the Commonwealth's Sex
  18|                                                       Offender Registry Board that the sex offender has violated a town bylaw.
  19|                       Section 9. Safety Zone
  20|                              A. Prohibitions
  21|                        A sex offender who has been finally classified as a Level 2 or 3 offender pursuant to the guidelines of the Sex
  22|                        Offender Registry Board, and for as long as so classified, is prohibited from entering upon the premises of a school
  23|                       or day-care center unless previously authorized specifically in writing by the school administration or day-care
  24|                       center owner.
  25|                        A sex offender who has been finally classified as a Level 2 or 3 offender pursuant to the guidelines of the Sex
  26|                       Offender Registry Board, and for as long as so classified, is prohibited from entering upon the premises of an elderly
  27|                       housing facility, over 55 Community or Senior Citizens Center, unless previously authorized in writing by the on-
  28|                       site manager of the elderly housing facility, over 55 Community or Senior Citizen Center.
  29|                        A sex offender who has been finally classified as a Level 2 or 3 offender pursuant to the guidelines of the Sex
  30|                        Offender Registry Board, and for as long as so classified, is prohibited from entering upon the premises of a park or
  31|                       any recreational facility. A sex offender who has been finally classified as a Level 2 or 3 offender pursuant to the
  32|                       guidelines of the Sex Offender Registry Board, and for as long as so classified, after having received notice from
  33|                       the Lunenburg Police Department that he/she is loitering by having remained for more than fifteen (15) minutes
  34|                       within five hundred (500) feet of a public or private school, park, playground, beach, biking/hiking trail, other
  35|                       recreational facility, elderly housing facility, over 55 community, senior citizens center, or licensed day-care center,
  36|                       is prohibited from continuing to so loiter. For purposes of determining the minimum distance separation under this
  37|                       section, the distance shall be measured by following a straight line from the registered sex offender to the outer
  38|                       property line of the public or private school, park, playground, beach, biking/hiking trail, other recreational facility,
  39|                        elderly housing facility, over 55 community, senior citizens center, or licensed day-care center.
  40|                        A sex offender who has been finally classified as a Level 2 or 3 offender pursuant to the guidelines of the Sex
  41|                       Offender Registry Board, and for as long as so classified after having received notice from the Lunenburg Police
  42|                       Department that he/she is loitering by having remained for more than fifteen (15) minutes within five hundred (500)
  43|                        feet of a school and/or camp bus stop which has been designated in a list maintained by the Town and available to
  44|                        the public is prohibited from continuing to so loiter; provided, however, that this prohibition shall not apply on days
  45|                       when the schools and/or camps within the Town of Lunenburg are not in session.
  46|                              A. Exceptions
  47|                              1) The prohibitions defined in this bylaw shall not be construed or enforced so as to prohibit a sex offender
  48|                                    from exercising his or her right to vote in any federal, state or municipal election, conducting town and/or
  49|                                    police business or from attending any religious service.
  50|                              2) The prohibitions defined in this bylaw do not apply to a sex offender's place of residence when such
  51|                                    residence is accepted under this bylaw.
  52|                              B. Penalties
  53|                                    1) Criminal Complaint. Violation of the safety zone provisions of this bylaw may be enforced by
  54|                                         criminal complaint filed by any police officer of the Town of Lunenburg. Each day a violation exists
  55|                                          shall constitute a separate violation. The fine for each violation, upon conviction, shall be three
  56|                                         hundred dollars ($300).
  57|                                                                                                    178

===PAGE 179=== (ocr, 43 lines)
   1|                                    2) Noncriminal Disposition. In addition to enforcement by criminal complaint, violation of the safety zone
   2|                                   provisions of this bylaw may be enforced through any lawful means in law or in equity by any police
   3|                                   officer of the Town of Lunenburg including, but not limited to, enforcement by non-criminal disposition
   4|                                   pursuant to G.L. c. 40, § 21D. Each day a violation exists shall constitute a separate violation. The
   5|                                   penalties for noncriminal disposition shall be as follows:
   6|                       a) First offense: noncriminal fine of one hundred and fifty dollars ($150), enforceable by a Lunenburg police officer.
   7|                       b) Subsequent offense: noncriminal fine of three hundred dollars ($300), enforceable by a Lunenburg police officer,
   8|                       and written notification to the offender's parole officer and/or probation officer, and the Commonwealth's Sex
   9|                       Offender Registry Board that the sex offender has violated a Town Bylaw.
  10|                       Section 10. Maps and List of Safety Zones
  11|                       One or more maps depicting the prohibited residency restriction areas defined by this bylaw and depicting the safety
  12|                       zone areas defined by this bylaw shall be created by the Town and maintained by the Lunenburg Police Department.
  13|                       A written list describing the prohibited areas defined by this bylaw, including school and/or camp bus stops, shall be
  14|                       created by the Town and maintained by the Lunenburg Police Department. As to school and/or camps bus stops, the
  15|                       list shall govern over the maps. The list, maps and a copy of this bylaw shall be available to the public at the
  16|                       Lunenburg Police Department, the Lunenburg Town Clerk's office and on the Town of Lunenburg's website. The
  17|                        Town shall review the list and maps annually for changes.
  18|                       Section 11. Severability
  19|                       If any portion of this bylaw is deemed by a court of competent jurisdiction to be unconstitutional or otherwise
  20|                       invalid or unenforceable, such judgment shall not impair or invalidate or render unenforceable the remaining
  21|                       portions of this bylaw. (Submitted by Police Chief) Board of Selectmen to make recommendation at ATM, Finance
  22|                       Committee reports no direct financial impact.

  41|                       Whalom Lake.
  42|                       Table of Contents
  43|                       Section 1. Purpose and Scope
  44|                       Section 2. Definitions
  45|                       Section 3. Operation of Snow Vehicles and All-Terrain Vehicles
  46|                       Section 4. Operation of Motor Vehicles prohibited
  47|                       Section 5. Access
  48|                       Section 6. Penalties
  49|                                                                                                    180

===PAGE 181=== (ocr, 59 lines)
   1|                       Section 1. Purpose and Scope
   2|                       The purpose and scope of this bylaw is to protect the safety of the public, to prevent the destruction of aquatic life, waterfowl
   3|                       or other wildlife, the decay of water quality and damage to abutting private and public lands by the inappropriate use of
   4|                       motor vehicles, recreation vehicles or snow vehicles on the waters or frozen waters of Whalom Lake; to promote voluntary
   5|                       compliance with all applicable laws relating to the operation of motor vehicles and when necessary to deter noncompliance
   6|                       through fines and penalties.
   7|                       Section 2. Definitions
   8|                             a) Motor Vehicle: any motor vehicle as defined in M.G.L Chapter 90, § 1.
   9|                             b) All-terrain vehicle: means a motorized recreational vehicle designed or modified for travel on four low pressure
  10|                                   tires and having a seat designed to be straddled by the operator and handlebars for steering control, and recreational
  11|                                   vehicle or off-highway vehicle as defined in CMR 323, § 3.02 and governed by M.G.L Chapter 90B.
  12|                                 Snow vehicle: a motor vehicle designed to travel over ice or snow, having a curb weight of not more than 453
  13|                                   kilograms or 1000 pounds, driven by track or tracks in contact with the snow or ice and steered by a ski or skis in
  14|                                   contact with the snow or ice as defined in CMR 323, & 302 and governed by M.G.L Chapter 90B.
  15|                                   Operation: to ride in or on and control the operation of, or to maintain, suffer, supervise, or permit the operation of,
  16|                                   or to push a snow vehicle or an all- terrain vehicle, or in the case of a motor vehicle, any person who makes use of
  17|                                   any mechanical or electrical agency, which alone or in sequence will set in motion the motive power of the vehicle,
  18|                                   or if the engine is not running, any person who utilizes any combination of actions that would set the vehicle in
  19|                                   motion.
  20|                            e)  Public Access: shall mean the public access located in the City of Leominster or any other place where Whalom
  21|                                   Lake can be accessed by the public.
  22|                             f) Law Enforcement Officer: any police officer, constable or other officer authorized to make arrests or serve process
  23|                                   provided he is in uniform or displays his/her badge of office.
  24|                                 Board: Town of Lunenburg, Board of Selectmen
  25|                       Section 3. Operation of Snow Vehicles and All-Terrain Vehicles
  26|                             A. No person, or group of persons shall operate, or cause to be operated on the waters or frozen waters of Whalom
  27|                                   Lake, any snow vehicles that are not in compliance with Massachusetts CMR 323 § 2.01 to 3.09 & M.G.L. c. 90
  28|                                   § 21 to 35.
  29|                             B.    When the Town of Lunenburg or any other agency or state agency duly authorized by law has posted the waters or
  30|                                   frozen waters of Whalom Lake to prohibit access for or use of snow vehicles or all-terrain vehicles, no person, or
  31|                                   group of persons shall operate any snow vehicle or all-terrain vehicle upon such waters or frozen waters. In the
  32|                                  absence of such a posting, persons utilizing water or the frozen water of Whalom Lake do so at their own risk and
  33|                                  the Town of Lunenburg assumes no responsibility either implied or expressed for the safety of any person who
  34|                                   voluntarily assumes a known and obvious risk inherent in such activities. No person shall operate a snow vehicle or
  35|                                   all-terrain vehicle upon any frozen waters of Whalom Lake under any circumstance unless a minimum of five inches
  36|                                   of solid ice cover is present. The operator shall determine the thickness of the ice and assumes all responsibility in
  37|                                   undertaking an activity with an inherent and known risk.
  38|                       Section 4. Operation of Motor Vehicles Prohibited
  39|                             A. No person, group of persons or organizations shall operate, or cause to be operated, any motor vehicle as defined in
  40|                                   M.G.L. c. 90 § 1 on the waters or frozen waters of Whalom Lake.
  41|                       Section 5. Access
  42|                             B. No snow vehicle or all-terrain vehicle shall enter upon Whalom Lake except by public access or by written
  43|                                   permission by the landowner.
  44|                       Section 6. Penalties
  45|                       This bylaw may be enforced through any lawful means in law or in equity including, but not limited to, enforcement by
  46|                       criminal complaint pursuant to G.L. c.40 § 21D, by the Board of Selectmen, the Town Manager, or their duly authorized
  47|                       agents, or any police officer. The fine for a violation of this bylaw shall be three hundred dollars ($300.) for each offense.
  48|                       (Submitted by Police Chief) Board of Selectmen recommends approval. Finance Committee reports no direct financial
  49|                       impact. VOTED with amendment to Section 3.B adding the words "In the absence of such a posting," to the beginning
  50|                       of the second sentence.
