  44|                        Article I. Buyers and Sellers of Goods and Electronics
  45|                       Section I. Licensing Authority and Requirements
  46|                       Subsection A.
  47|                       The Board of Selectmen may license suitable persons to be pawnbrokers or buyers of goods pursuant to law. Licenses shall
  48|                       expire on the last day of December annually no matter when obtained during the preceding year. Such licenses shall not be
  49|                       valid to protect the holders thereof in a building or place other than that designated in the license, unless consent to removal
  50|                       is granted by the Board of Selectmen. Applications for new licenses under the rule may be filed at any time with the Board of
  51|                       Selectmen. Applications for the reissue of licenses already existing should be filed at least 30 days before the expiration of
  52|                       such licenses. Persons whose licenses have expired and have not been reissued will be liable to prosecution if carrying on
  53|                       business for which the license is required. Every person so licensed shall, at the time of receiving such license, file a bond as
  54|                       provided by M.G.L. c. 140 § 77 as amended.
  55|                                                                                                    182

===PAGE 183=== (ocr, 45 lines)
   1|                       Subsection B.
   2|                       Persons who engage in or carry on the business of lending money on mortgages, deposits or pledges of wearing apparel,
   3|                       jewelry, ornaments, household goods or other personal property, or of purchasing such property on condition of selling the
   4|                       same back again at a stipulated price, when the property so mortgaged, pledged or purchased is deposited with the lender,
   5|                       must be licensed as pawnbrokers. This provision, however, does not apply to loans made on stocks, bonds, notes or other
   6|                       written or printed evidence of ownership of property or of indebtedness to the holder or owner of such securities. (M.G.L. c.
   7|                       140, 8 70- 85)
   8|                       Section II. Interest Rates
   9|                             A. Licensed pawnbrokers may charge interest at the rate of 3% per month, and in no event may they charge more than
  10|                                  the rate allowed by the Massachusetts Commissioner of Banks.
  11|                             B. No such pawnbrokers shall charge or receive any greater rate of interest, and interest shall be determined on the
  12|                                  precise sum advanced by the lender.
  13|                             C. No pawnbroker shall make or receive any extra charge or fee for storage, care or safekeeping of any goods, articles
  14|                                   or things pawned with him. (M.G.L. c. 140, 8 78)
  15|                       Section III. Police may enter and inspect premises and records
  16|                       Any officer of the Lunenburg Police may at any time enter upon any premises used by a licensed pawnbroker or buyer for the
  17|                       purposes of his or her business, ascertain how he or she conducts his or her business and examine all articles taken in pawn or
  18|                       bought, or kept or stored in or upon said premises and all books and inventories shall be exhibited to any above name
  19|                       whenever a demand shall be made for such exhibition. (M.G.L. c. 140, 874) (Penalty for refusal, M.G.L. c. 140, 874)
  20|                       Section IV. Numbering of pawned articles
  21|                       Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall at the time of making any loan, attach a number to the article taken in pawn or
  22|                       bought and shall make entry of such number in the book provided for in Section V. of this article.
  23|                       Section V. Maintenance of records; contents; photo identification
  24|                               A. Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall keep a book of style and size in which shall be legibly written in ink in
  25|                                    the English language at the time of making each loan, an account and description, including all distinguishing
  26|                                    marks and numbers and serial numbers of the goods, articles or things pledged or pawned, the amount of money
  27|                                    loaned or paid thereon, the day and hour when it was pawned, the rate of interest to be paid on such loan and the
  28|                                    number of such article as same. No entry made in said book shall be erased, obliterated or defaced. Electronic
  29|                                    record keeping by the pawnbroker or buyer is acceptable as long as the records meet all the bylaw requirements.
  30|                              B. Every pawnbroker or buyer shall photograph any person pawning or pledging articles and keep such photographs
  31|                                    with said books as part of his or her records. (M.G.L. c. 140, 8 79).
  32|                               C. For all transactions, every pawnbroker or buyer shall also require positive identitication and shall record the type of
  33|                                    identification presented and record the date of birth from any person pawning, pledging or selling any article.
  34|                                    Positive identification shall mean any picture identification card issued by a governmental agency.
  35|                       Section VI. Pledge cards; contents; retention
  36|                       Each pledger shall be required by the pawnbroker to sign his/her name and age and address on a card. In the event that the
  37|                       pledger is unable to write, the pawnbroker shall fill in the name, age and address on such card, together with a notation
  38|                       stating that the pledger was unable to do so. Such card shall be retained seven years in an alphabetical index file by the
  39|                       licensed pawnbrokers.
  40|                       Section VII. Copy of required record to pledger
  41|                       Every pawnbroker or buyer shall at the time of making such loan deliver to the person who pawns or pledges any goods,
  42|                       articles or things, a memorandum or note signed by him, containing the substance of the entry required to be made in his
  43|                       book by the provisions of Section V. and no charge shall be made or required by any pawnbroker or buyer for any such entry,
  44|                       memorandum or note. (M.G.L. c. 140, 8 80)
  45|                                                                                                    183

===PAGE 184=== (ocr, 54 lines)
   1|                       Section VIII. Daily report to police
   2|                           Subsection A. Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall make out and deliver a report of transactions to the Lunenburg
   3|                       Police Chief or his designee every day before the hour of 10:00 a.m., a legible and correct list containing an accurate
   4|                       description, including all distinguishable marks, numbers and serial numbers of all articles taken in pawn or bought during
   5|                       the preceding business day, the respective numbers of such articles as provided by Section IV. of this bylaw, the amount
   6|                       loaned or paid thereon and the time when such articles were pawned or bought. This report can be done electronically, via the
   7|                       Internet, or faxed to the Lunenburg Police Chief or his designee. If during the preceding day no articles have been taken in by
   8|                       such pawnbroker or buyer, he or she is required to report affirmatively. This report can be done both electronically via the
   9|                       Internet and by fax.
  10|                          Subsection B. If any goods or articles pawned or pledged and in the possession of a pawnbroker or buyer are subsequently
  11|                       determined to be stolen property by a member of the Lunenburg Police Department or the Massachusetts State Police, or if
  12|                       the rightful owner identifies property in the possession of a pawnbroker or buyer and the property so identified is confirmed
  13|                       to be stolen goods by a member of the Lunenburg Police Department or Massachusetts State Police, said property shall be
  14|                       returned to the rightful owner at no cost to such owner.
  15|                       Section IX. Posting Requirements
  16|                          Subsection A. Every licensed pawnbroker or buyer shall post in a conspicuous place in his or her shop or office a copy of
  17|                       the statutes, ordinances and police regulations relating to pawnbrokers/buyers, to be furnished by the Lunenburg Police
  18|                       Department's Police Chief or designee, and shall put in some suitable and conspicuous place in his shop a sign having his/her
  19|                       name and occupation legibly inscribed thereon in large lettering.
  20|                          Subsection B. No pawnbroker or buyer shall place or maintain any signs or devices upon or in connection with his or her
  21|                       licensed premises indicating or tending to indicate that any form of business is conducted therein which he or she is not
  22|                       legally authorized to pursue.
  23|                       Section X. Hours of Operation
  24|                       Pawnbroker or buyer may have his/her shop open for transactions between sunrise and 10:00 p.m. in the evening of any
  25|                        weekday and weekend. Under no circumstances can a pawnbroker or buyer operate after the hour of 10:00 p.m. to sunrise.
  26|                       Section XI. Disposition of pledged articles
  27|                          Subsection A. Articles deposited in pawn with a licensed pawnbroker shall unless redeemed, be retained by him/her on the
  28|                       premises occupied by him/her for their business for at least four months after the date of deposit.
  29|                          Subsection B. After the expiration of the applicable period of time he/she may sell the article by public auction, apply the
  30|                       proceeds thereof in satisfaction of the debt or demand and the expense of the notice and sale and pay any surplus to the
  31|                       person entitled thereto on demand.
  32|                          Subsection C. No such sale of any article which is not of a perishable nature shall be made unless not less than 10 days
  33|                       prior to the sale a written notice of the intended sale shall have been sent by registered mail to the person entitled to the
  34|                       payment of any surplus as aforesaid, addressed to his residence as appearing in the records of such pawnbrokers. Proof of
  35|                       registered mail shall be kept on file for one year after the date of sale.
  36|                          Subsection D. No article taken in pawn by such pawnbroker or buyer shall be disposed of otherwise than as above
  37|                       provided, any agreement or contract between the parties thereto to the contrary notwithstanding.
  38|                          Subsection E. Articles of personal apparel shall not be deemed to be of a perishable nature within the meaning of this
  39|                       section. (M.G.L. c. 140, 8 71)
  40|                       Section XII. Prohibitions
  41|                          Subsection A. No pawnbroker or buyer shall make a loan, directly or indirectly, to a person under the age of 18, knowing
  42|                       or having reason to believe him or her to be such.
  43|                          Subsection B. No pawnbroker or buyer shall loan money secured by deposit or pledge of a firearm, rifle, shotgun or
  44|                       machine gun. (M.G.L. c. 140, § 131B)
  45|                          Subsection C. No pawnbroker or buyer shall hold a license to sell, rent, or lease a firearm, rifle, shotgun, or machine gun.
  46|                       Section XIlI. Complaints, Disciplinary Action; Hearing
  47|                          Subsection A. Complaints concerning licensed pawnbrokers or buyers shall be investigated by the Lunenburg Police
  48|                        Department under the direction of the Chief of Police. The Chief of Police or his designee will provide a disciplinary request
  49|                       to the Board of Selectmen for actionable complaints lodged against licensees.
  50|                          Subsection B. In the event the Chief of Police determines that disciplinary action should be instituted against a licensed
  51|                       pawnbroker or buyer, the Chief of Police shall cause to be served upon the licensed pawnbroker or buyer notice as to the
  52|                       time, date and place of hearing and of the charge with a statement of the reasons for the proposed disciplinary action.
  53|                       Hearings shall be conducted in accordance with law.
  54|                                                                                                    184

===PAGE 185=== (ocr, 54 lines)
   1|                       Section XIV. Suspension or Revocation of License
   2|                       The Board of Selectmen may suspend or revoke licenses provided for by this article for any cause which the Board of
   3|                       Selectmen deems sufficient. Offenses which may result in the suspension or revocation of a pawnbroker's or buyer's license
   4|                       include but are not limited to the following:
   5|                       a) A violation of any section of this article.
   6|                       b) A violation of any provision of any statute or applicable law.
   7|                       Article II. Sale, Exchange or Purchase of Metals
   8|                       Section I. Findings
   9|                       The Town of Lunenburg finds that there is a cognizable risk for stolen metals to end up in the possession of even legitimate
  10|                       businesses which trade in metals, including precious metals. Certain criminals bring stolen metals, including precious metals
  11|                       to dealers in jewelry and scrap metal. The victims of theft have only small hope of recovering their property unless the people
  12|                       and entities who receive scrap metals and jewelry are regulated in a manner which identifies both the metal received by the
  13|                       dealers and the persons who deliver the metal to these dealers. There is an Internet alert system used by the Lunenburg Police
  14|                       Department which reports stolen metals. Monitoring transactions within the town and identifying both the metals and the
  15|                       persons selling or delivering these metals will serve both to deter theft and to enable the Lunenburg Police Department to
  16|                       trace and recover stolen property and return it to the rightful owners.
  17|                       Section II. Definitions
  18|                       As used in Article II, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:
  19|                       ARTICLE: Any metal which is subject to Article II and is exchanged, sold, collected, bartered or received by a person
  20|                       dealing in metals.
  21|                       CHIEF OF POLICE: The Chief of the Lunenburg Police Department or his designee.
  22|                       EXCHANGE: Receiving, purchasing, selling or bartering metals, including precious metals and industrial scrap metals.
  23|                       METAL: A chemical element that is malleable, opaque and ductile, usually solid, which has a characteristic luster, is a good
  24|                       conductor of heat and electricity, and can be melted or fused, hammered into thin sheets, or drawn into wires, e.g., copper,
  25|                       aluminum, gold, silver or iron or other metals.
  26|                       PRECIOUS METAL(S): Any metal which is considered valuable, such as silver, gold, platinum and copper without regard
  27|                       to the form or amount of such precious metal.
  28|                       BOARD: Board of Selectmen
  29|                       Section III. License Required
  30|                       a) No person shall collect, deal in, exchange, buy, or keep a shop or place for the exchange, purchase, sale or barter of metals,
  31|                       including precious metals and industrial metals, in any building or place within the limits of the town without having a
  32|                       license issued by the Board of Selectman. The license requirement and the other requirements of this Article II shall not
  33|                       apply to commercial haulers having valid, current United States Department of Transportation stickers affixed to their
  34|                       vehicles.
  35|                       b) Board of Selectmen may for a fee set by said board and based upon an application devised by said board, license suitable
  36|                       persons to be dealers in and keepers of shops or locations for the purchase, sale or barter of precious metals at such places
  37|                       within the town as may be designated in such license. The Board of Selectmen may place reasonable conditions on such
  38|                       licenses which shall be inscribed on the face of the license. A license shall be limited to a specific address stated thereon.
  39|                       Subject to the notice and appeal provisions contained in Section IX (E),(2), (3) of this Article II, the Board of Selectmen may
  40|                       deny a license to any person who in the exercise of his reasonable discretion is unsuitable.
  41|                       c) All metal dealer licenses shall expire annually on the last day in December. The license holders shall be responsible for
  42|                       submitting an application for license renewal with the license fee to the Board of Selectmen at least 30 days prior to the last
  43|                       day in December. Upon receipt of an application for renewal, the Board shall consider the performance of the licensee during
  44|                       the previous year and shall determine whether the licensee had been found in violation of this Article II and other ordinances
  45|                       and regulations of the town applicable to metal dealers.
  46|                       d) The Board of Selectmen may promulgate reasonable regulations not inconsistent with this Article II which shall be binding
  47|                       upon all licensees. No regulation shall take effect until the expiration of 30 days from the date the regulation(s) is delivered or
  48|                       mailed to the person(s) then licensed. The Board of Selectmen shall deliver a complete set of regulations and any
  49|                       amendments thereto to the Town Clerk. The Town Clerk shall maintain the complete set of all regulations in a book available
  50|                       to the public.
  51|                       e) The obligation to obtain a license as required by this section will take effect 45 days after it is finally enacted.
  52|                       Section IV. Transactions with Minors
  53|                        No licensee shall, directly or indirectly, exchange any metals with a person under the age of 18.
  54|                                                                                                    185

===PAGE 186=== (ocr, 52 lines)
   1|                        Section V. Waiting Period
   2|                        No article exchanged, purchased or received shall be sold, or altered in appearance, form or substance until a period of at
   3|                        least twenty-one (21) days have elapsed from the date of its purchase or receipt. All articles exchanged, purchased or received
   4|                        must be made available to the Lunenburg Police Department upon request within 24 hours of such request, and the Police
   5|                        Department may investigate to determine if any article is or may be stolen property. This waiting period does not apply to
   6|                        scrap metal yards which are exempt from any waiting period.
   7|                        Section VI. Daily Report
   8|                        Every licensee shall electronically create and send to the Police Chief or his designee on a form, in the manner and at the time
   9|                        prescribed by the Police Chief or his designee, a legible complete list containing an accurate description of all metal articles
  10|                        received by the licensee during the previous 24 hours. The description must include: the type of metal, the size and/or
  11|                        quantity, whether the article is or may be a precious metal, if applicable; whether the article is typically used by or associated
  12|                        with a male or female, the wording of any engraving, whether the article has any gems or precious stones, any identifying
  13|                        number and every other identifiable trait.
  14|                        Section VII. Recordkeeping Requirements
  15|                        A. Every licensee shall, at the time of making any exchange or receipt of any article, assign and attach a number
  16|                           to each article received and shall make entry of such number in the book described in Subsection B.
  17|                        B. Every licensee shall keep a book in which shall be legibly written in ink, in the English language, at the time
  18|                            the licensee receives any article, the following information:
  19|                          1) An account and description, including all distinguishing or identifying marks and numbers of every article
  20|                            received by the licensee.
  21|                          2) The amount of money, if any, paid for the article.
  22|                          3) The date and hour when it was received.
  23|                          4) The name, age, permanent address and telephone number of the person from who purchased or received.
  24|                          5) A copy of the document used to identify the person giving the article to the licensee.
  25|                        C. Every licensee shall require positive identification from any person selling or exchanging any article. The
  26|                           licensee shall copy and record the type of identification presented and the date of birth from any person giving
  27|                           or exchanging any article. Positive identification means only a government-issued document with the person's
  28|                           name and photograph. The licensee shall photograph any person exchanging any articles). A copy of the
  29|                           identification and the photograph shall be kept with the book required by this section as part of his records.
  30|                        D. No entry made in the book required by this section shall be erased, obliterated or defaced in any manner
  31|                           whatsoever. The book shall at all times be open for the inspection by the Police Chief or any police officer.
  32|                           The licensee shall keep and maintain all the records required by this Article II for a period of three years from
  33|                           the date of the last entry in any book.
  34|                        Section VIII. Posting of Name, Occupation and License; Inspections
  35|                        Every licensee shall post in some suitable and conspicuous place where he or she receives or exchanges articles, a sign
  36|                        having his/ her full legal name, and his/her business name, if different, and his/her occupation legibly described thereon in
  37|                       large letters. The current license shall also be so posted. The location where transactions occur, the store or shop and all
  38|                        articles exchanged and or kept therein or received therein and the book and documents required by this Article II, may at all
  39|                        times be examined by the Police Chief or any police officer at their request.
  40|                        Section IX. Violations and Penalties
  41|                        A. Whoever not having a valid license as required by this Article II, exchanges, collects, deals in or barters metals in any
  42|                        place or manner other than that designated in his license, or after notice to him that his license has been revoked, or whoever
  43|                        violates this Article II or any rule, regulation or restriction contained in his license, or any regulation promulgated by the
  44|                        Town of Lunenburg shall be subject to the fines and sanctions described in this section. Each day of such violation shall
  45|                        constitute a separate offense.
  46|                        B. The fine for breach of the duty imposed by this Article II is three hundred dollars ($300). Each day on which the person
  47|                        continues in violation shall be considered as a separate violation.
  48|                        C. This Article II may at the discretion of the Chief of Police be enforced by civil process or by noncriminal disposition as
  49|                        provided in M.G.L. c. 40, § 21D. The Chief of Police or any Lunenburg police officer may issue tickets to enforce this
  50|                        Article II. If enforced civilly by ticket each day on which a violation exists shall be deemed to be a separate offense and the
  51|                        violator shall be subject to the following fines:
  52|                                                                                                    186

===PAGE 187=== (ocr, 51 lines)
   1|                       1) First violation: $150.
   2|                             2) Second violation: $200.
   3|                             3) Third violation: $300.
   4|                             4) Fourth and each subsequent violation: $300.
   5|                       D. In addition to the penalties set forth above, the enforcing authority may seek an injunction from an appropriate court to
   6|                       restrain any violation of this Article II, any regulation promulgated by the Town of Lunenburg or any condition inscribed on
   7|                       a license.
   8|                       E. The Board of Selectmen may terminate any license or refuse to renew any license for violation of this Article II, a
   9|                       regulation promulgated by the Town of Lunenburg or any condition inscribed on the license. The Board of Selectmen shall
  10|                       use the procedure described in this section.
  11|                            1) Notice of violation. Whenever it comes to the attention of the Board of Selectmen that a violation of this Article II, a
  12|                       regulation promulgated by the Town of Lunenburg or a condition inscribed on a license, the Board shall by written notice,
  13|                       deliver personally or send by certified mail to the licensee notifying him of the violation and order the person to cease and
  14|                       desist. Depending on the severity of the violation as determined by him, the Board of Selectmen may terminate the license.
  15|                       The Board shall also provide notice described herein if it denies an application for a license stating the reasons therefor.
  16|                            2) Contents of notice. The written notice to the licensee shall contain a description of the violation(s) and the date(s) of
  17|                       occurrence and a citation to the section of the ordinance, regulation or license condition which the licensee is alleged to have
  18|                       violated. The notice will, if applicable, describe what the licensee must do to comply, whether the Board of Selectmen
  19|                       intends to terminate the license and the effective date of the termination which shall afford the licensee at least seven days to
  20|                       file an appeal of the proposed termination with the Board. In the case of denial of a license, the notice shall state the reasons
  21|                           3) Appeal. Upon receipt of a notice of license termination, or denial, the licensee may, within seven days of receipt of the
  22|                       notice, file a written appeal by delivery or certified mail to the Board of Selectmen's office during the hours of 8:30 a.m. to
  23|                       4:30 p.m. on days when Town Hall is open for business. When the Board of Selectmen receives an appeal, they shall appoint
  24|                       a neutral hearing officer who will take testimony from any persons with knowledge of the facts including any police officer
  25|                       and the appellant. The appellant may be represented by counsel and any person so testifying will be subject to cross
  26|                       examination. The proceedings will be governed by the rules of evidence applicable to an informal administrative hearing. The
  27|                       hearing officer will assure that an appropriate record, including any documents submitted, is made and kept. The decision of
  28|                       the hearing officer will be written and final.
  29|                       F. The Board of Selectmen, subject to the process described in this section, may refuse to renew any license. The Board shall
  30|                       not issue a license to any person convicted of a felony.
  31|                       Section X. License and Administration Fees

  33|                                 2) Second Buyer of Metal and Precious Metals Annually $250.00

  34|                       PREAMBLE
  35|                       This by-law establishes a Salary Administration Plan, hereinafter called the "Plan", which classifies several positions of town
  36|                       services into groups, establishes salary schedules, establishes so called "fringe" benefits, or "indirect pay" provisions, such as
  37|                       holidays and vacations with pay, sick leave, and the like, and establishes a Personnel Committee to administer the Plan, as
  38|                       hereinafter provided, and to represent the interest of both taxpayers and town employees.
  39|                       SECTION 1. THE PERSONNEL COMMITTEE
  40|                       There is hereby established a Personnel Committee consisting of five members, each residing in the Town of Lunenburg, to
  41|                       be appointed by the Selectmen and Town Manager, and each member shall serve for a term of three years; provided,
  42|                       however, that of the members originally appointed, one shall serve a term of one year, two for a term of two years, and two
  43|                       for a term of three years, as designated by the Selectmen and Town Manager. However, nothing herein shall be deemed to
  44|                       prohibit the chairman of the Personnel Committee from designating a member of said committee to serve ex officio as
  45|                       representative of said Committee on a study committee of the Town Meeting, nor shall such service affect the tenure of said
  46|                       member of the Personnel Committee. If any member of the Personnel Committee shall resign or otherwise vacate the office
  47|                       before the expiration of their term, the successor shall be appointed by the Selectmen and Town Manager, at their discretion,
  48|                       to serve for the balance of the unexpired term.
  49|                        A Town employee may serve as an ex officio member of the Personnel Committee and may be called upon from time to time
  50|                       to provide information requested by the Personnel Committee so that the Personnel Committee can make well informed
  51|                       decisions and proposals.
  52|                       Said Committee shall elect its own chairman and vice-chairman by September 15" of each year; and in the absence or
  53|                       incapacity of the chairman, the vice-chairman shall act as chairman. The Committee shall keep a record of its official
  54|                       proceedings and actions, may establish its own rule of procedure and may, subject to appropriation therefore, retain such
  55|                                                                                                    189

===PAGE 190=== (ocr, 44 lines)
   1|                        clerical and other assistance, and make such other expenditures as may be necessary to the performance of its duties. Three
   2|                        members shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of the business of the committee, and the affirmative vote of three
   3|                        members shall be necessary to any official act of the Committee.
   4|                        The Personnel Committee is hereby authorized to administer the provisions of this by-law, except for such duties as may be
   5|                        specifically assigned by statute or by-law to other Town officers, boards or committees. Appeals for decisions of the
   6|                        Personnel Committee may be taken to the Town at the next Annual or Special Town Meeting.
   7|                        The Personnel Committee may from time to time issue, amend, or revoke Administrative Orders for the purpose of giving
   8|                        effect to the provisions of this by-law, and for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of such other by-laws and votes
   9|                        of the Town, pertaining to personnel administration, as said Committee may be responsible for administering and/or
  10|                        enforcing. Each such order shall be numbered in sequence, and said Committee shall maintain in the Town Office a file for
  11|                        all such orders issued, said file to be open to public inspection.
  12|                        Except as otherwise provided by law, the Committee shall have access to all facts, figures, records and other information
  13|                        relating to the personnel of Town departments other than the School Department, and the same shall be furnished forthwith
  14|                        by any such department whenever so requested by the Personnel Committee, in such a form as said Committee may require.
  15|                       In the event that the Personnel Committee does not have enough members to conduct business, the Town Manager shall have
  16|                       the authority to administer the Salary Administration Plan.
  17|                       SECTION 2. CLASSIFICATION AND SALARY SCHEDULE
  18|                        The positions of all officers except those part-time administrative positions required by statute, and employees in the service
  19|                        of the Town, whether probationary, full-time, part-time, hourly, seasonal, intermittent, and any others, other than those
  20|                       positions filled by popular election, all contractual employees, all police officers under the rank of Police Chief, and those
  21|                       under the direction and control of the School Committee, are hereby classified by titles in the groups listed in Schedule A,
  22|                        entitled "Classification and Salary Schedule", as set forth in this by-law.
  23|                       SECTION 3. TITLE OF POSITIONS
  24|                       No person shall be appointed, employed or paid as an employee in any position subject to the provision of the Salary
  25|                        payrolls, budget estimates and official reports, and in every other connection involving personnel and fiscal processes.
  26|                       SECTION 4. NEW OR CHANGED POSITIONS
  27|                        The Personnel Committee tentatively may add new job title and descriptions to this Plan, establishing grades with minimum
  28|                        and maximum wage or salary brackets for the same, and reclassifying existing jobs, revising the description and the
  29|                        minimum and maximum wage and salary brackets therefore, and such addition or reclassification to be effective only for the
  30|                        period from the date of such action by the Personnel Committee to the date of any vote with respect thereto adopted at a
  31|                       subsequent Town Meeting but in no case later than the next Annual Town Meeting unless such later date as may be specified
  32|                       by such vote. Any increase in wages or salaries under this section shall be effective only if funds are available for the
  33|                        purpose, and approved by the Finance Committee and Board of Selectmen.
  34|                       SECTION 5. RECLASSIFICATION OF EMPLOYEES
  35|                       No employee shall be reclassified to a job in another group, either higher or lower, until the Personnel Committee shall have
  36|                        determined that such a reclassification will be consistent with the provisions of the Salary Administration Plan.
  37|                       SECTION 6. JOB DESCRIPTIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS
  38|                       The Personnel Committee shall maintain written job descriptions of the jobs or positions in the Plan, describing the essential
  39|                       functions, requirements and duties. The descriptions shall not be interpreted as either complete or restrictive and employees
  40|                        shall continue to perform any duties assigned by an employee's supervisor.
  41|                        Every three (3) years, the Personnel committee shall review the wage and salary schedules of all positions in the Plan, and be
  42|                       in a position to recommend to the Board of Selectmen any action deemed desirable to maintain a fair and equitable pay level.
  43|                       SECTION 7. SALARY SCHEDULE
  44|                                                                                                    190

===PAGE 191=== (ocr, 48 lines)
   1|                       The Classification and Salary Schedule of the Salary Administration Plan, set forth in Schedule A of this by-law, shall consist
   2|                       of the maximum and minimum salaries and step-rate salaries for the groups and positions in the Classification and Salary
   3|                       Schedule. The salary range of a group shall be the salary range for all positions classified in such group.
   4|                       Irrespective of the period of time for which pay rates may be shown in the Salary Schedule, all employees shall continue to
   5|                       be paid on an hourly, weekly, monthly, or other basis, as at present, unless otherwise authorized by the Personnel Committee
   6|                       or by amendment of the Salary Administration Plan.
   7|                       SECTION 8. SALARY RATES ABOVE MAXIMUM
   8|                        Any salary rate which is above the maximum rate for a job, as established by Salary Administration Plan, shall be deemed to
   9|                       be a personal rate, and apply only to the incumbent. When such incumbent leaves the employ of the Town or is transferred to
  10|                       another job with a higher maximum rate than their personal rate or higher maximum rates are established, the personal rate
  11|                       shall disappear. No other employee assigned to or hired for such job shall advance beyond the maximum of the job.
  12|                       SECTION 9. LAYOFF PROCEDURE - RECALL PROCEDURE
  13|                       Layoff Procedure - If the Town decides to lay off employees, it shall determine from which classification(s) or job
  14|                       function(s) layoffs shall be made. Layoffs shall then be made based on seniority within the classification.
  15|                       "Seniority" shall be the length of an employee's continuous service measured from the employee's most recent appointment
  16|                       date; provided an employee's seniority may be reduced for periods of unpaid leave, unless otherwise prohibited by law.
  17|                       If two or more employees in the same classification have the same seniority, the employee who has the shorter term of
  18|                       continuous employment with the Town shall be laid off. If there are two or more employees in the same classification with
  19|                       the same seniority and the same term of continuous employment with the Town, a part-time employee shall be laid off before
  20|                       a full-time employee. If there are still two or more employees in the same classification, the Town Manager shall determine
  21|                       which employee shall be laid off.
  22|                       An employee that is scheduled to be laid off shall have the right to bump other employees in lower classifications with less
  23|                       seniority, provided that the Town Manager, in his/her sole discretion, but with consultation of the Department Head, shall
  24|                       make a determination that the employee retained is qualified and able to perform the duties of the lower classification, subject
  25|                       to disability discrimination laws.
  26|                       Employees who have been laid off from employment are responsible for keeping the Town advised of their current address
  27|                       for the purpose of potential recall from layoff.
  28|                       Recall Policy - If the town conducts a recall from layoff, recall shall be offered in reverse order of layoff by classification
  29|                       provided the laid off employee is qualified and able to perform the duties of the classification to which the employee is being
  30|                       offered recall, subject to disability discrimination laws.
  31|                       Employees shall only be eligible for recall from layoff under the terms of this policy for one (1) year from the date of the
  32|                       employee's layoff.
  33|                       Any employee who is recalled from layoff under the terms of this policy shall retain his/her seniority, less the period of
  34|                       layoff.
  35|                       The Town will notify an employee of a recall opportunity by certified letter (or other verifiable method of delivery to the
  36|                       employee's last known address.             An employee who has been offered an opportunity to be recalled from layoff must advise
  37|                       the Town of his/her intention to accept recall within five (5) working days.
  38|                       SECTION 10. TRANSFERS AND PROMOTIONS
  39|                       (a) When an employee is promoted to a job with a higher rate range, or rate of pay, he/she shall enter it at the minimum of the
  40|                       job rate range or at their own rate, whichever is the higher, but in no event at a rate in excess of the maximum for such job.
  41|                       He/she may also receive at the time one or more step rate increases, provided the maximum for the job is not exceeded, if the
  42|                       Department Head recommends that qualification and performance warrant it, and the Personnel Committee approves. If the
  43|                       Department Head should feel that there should be a trial period before recommending the promotional step rate increase or
  44|                       increases, on recommendation of the Department Head, the Personnel Committee may approve any such deferred
  45|                       promotional increase at the conclusion of the trial period.
  46|                       (b)If an employee is transferred to a job with a lower rate range, or rate of pay, he/she shall enter it at their own rate or at the
  47|                       maximum rate for the job, whichever is the lower.
  48|                                                                                                    191

===PAGE 192=== (ocr, 51 lines)
   1|                       SECTION 11. NEW PERSONNEL
   2|                       (a) The hiring rate shall be the minimum of the rate range of the job for which the new employee if hired, unless otherwise
   3|                       authorized by the Personnel Committee. Department Heads shall notify the Personnel Committee of the hiring of all new
   4|                       personnel. This notification shall be done in writing via the New Hire Personnel Form.
   5|                       (b) Effective July 1, 2015, for new regular full-time, and new regular part-time personnel for whose position there is a rate
   6|                       range, eligibility for a step increase will depend on the employee's date of hire. If hired between January 1S and June 30"
   7|                       the employee is not eligible for a step increase until July 1s' of the following calendar year. If hired between July 1 and
   8|                       December 31", the employee is eligible for their first step increase on the upcoming July 1st
   9|                       SECTION 12. GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE
  10|                        Any employee who believes that they have received inequitable treatment is encouraged to discuss the grievance initially
  11|                       with their supervisor within 10 working days of the occurrence or knowledge of the event. If the employee is not
  12|                       comfortable discussing the matter with their direct supervisor, or if the matter is not settled, the employee should submit the
  13|                       said grievance to their Department Head. The Department Head shall meet with the employee and will respond in writing to
  14|                       the employee within 14 days of the meeting.
  15|                       meeting with the employee.
  16|                       SECTION 13. DEPARTMENT BUDGETS
  17|                       Each Department Head shall include in the annual budget request, a pay adjustment section to provide funds for anticipated
  18|                       pay adjustments during the ensuing year, expenditures to be made therefrom only in accordance with the Salary
  19|                       Administration Plan with approval of the Personnel Committee.
  20|                       SECTION 14. SEVERABILITY PROVISION
  21|                       In the event any provision of this by-law or application thereof shall be held to be invalid by the proper authorities, this shall
  22|                       not be construed to affect the validity of any other provision, or application thereof, of this by-law.
  23|                       SECTION 15. CIVIL SERVICE
  24|                       Nothing in this by-law of Salary Administration Plan shall be construed to conflict with Chapter 31 (Civil Service) of the
  25|                       General Laws.
  26|                       SECTION 16. HOURS OF WORK
  27|                       The schedule of hours to be worked shall be determined by the appropriate Department Head.
  28|                       For positions entitled to overtime pay at one and one-half (1 1/2) times the regular rate for work actually performed in excess
  29|                       of forty (40) hours within a work week, the words "work actually performed" shall be construed to include all duly paid time
  30|                       off, including but not limited to holidays, sick leave, vacation, personal days and bereavement leave, and such leave shall be
  31|                       included in the computation of forty (40) hours.
  32|                       Unauthorized leave or leave for which the employee is not entitled to compensation shall not be included in such
  33|                       computation.
  34|                       I.          Industrial Trades and Service Occupations
  35|                                   A.        Work Week 40 hours in 5 days.
  36|                                   B.      One and one-half (1 1/2) times the regular rate will be paid for work actually performed in
  37|                                              excess of forty (40) hours within a work week.
  38|                       II.         Office Occupations
  39|                                   A.        Work Week - Forty (40) hours in five days and may be reduced administratively to 36 hours in
  40|                                              four or five days.
  41|                                   B. One and one-half (1 1/2) times the regular rate will be paid for work actually performed in
  42|                                              excess of forty (40) hours within a work week.
  43|                       III.       Public Safety Occupations
  44|                                   A.         Fire Department - The hours of the Fire Department shall be determined by the Chief with the approval of
  45|                                              the Personnel Committee provided, however, that all hours worked by any member
  46|                                              of the Fire Department will be paid for at the regular rate then in force.
  47|                       IV.       Administrative and Professional Occupations
  48|                                   A.         Persons employed in these positions are not governed by hours of the positions under their
  49|                                              supervision or control. Generally, such positions shall be for at least forty (40) hours per week
  50|                                              when full-time and not entitled to overtime.
  51|                                                                                                    192

===PAGE 193=== (ocr, 51 lines)
   1|                       Notwithstanding anything in the foregoing paragraphs, the appropriate department head may, instead of paying the overtime
   2|                       rate, provide that the employee take compensatory time off at a rate of 1 1/2 times the hours worked that qualify for overtime
   3|                       pay. Compensatory time must be taken within 60 days.
   4|                       SECTION 17. PAID VACATIONS

   8|                       the prorated part-time employee's vacation day (See Section 28).

  26|                       shall be carried forward into a subsequent vacation year, nor shall any monetary compensation be given for such unused

  38|                                   worked since the preceding July 1.

  40|                       time or times as best serve the public interest, provided, however, that each employee shall be entitled to use at least 40 hours

  43|                       advance served the needs both of the employee and of the Town, it may be requested by the Department Head and authorized
  44|                       in writing by the Town Manager. In no case shall any such advanced vacation exceed the number of days for which the
  45|                       employee would be entitled to compensation, were he/she to terminate their services in good standing on the first day of such
  46|                       vacation, in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 5, subparagraph (b), of this section.
  47|                       SECTION 18. PAID HOLIDAYS
  48|                        The Town of Lunenburg shall observe the following holidays:
  49|                                   New Year's Day                                                     Columbus Day
  50|                                   Martin Luther King Day                                             Veterans' Day
  51|                                                                                                    193

===PAGE 194=== (ocr, 49 lines)
   1|                                   Washington's Birthday                                              Thanksgiving Day
   2|                                   Patriots Day                                                       The Day after Thanksgiving
   3|                                   Memorial Day                                                        The Day before Christmas
   4|                                   Independence Day                                                    Christmas Day
   5|                                   Labor Day
   6|                       It is the intent of this section that no employee, employed full-time or part-time for a minimum of twenty (20) hours, shall
   7|                       lose pay by the observance of any of the listed holidays; provided, however, that part-time employees shall receive holiday
   8|                       benefits only for holidays falling within their regularly scheduled work week; and provided further that, except as specifically
   9|                       provided elsewhere in this section, no employee, full-time or part-time, shall receive, in any week in which a holiday occurs,
  10|                       compensation in excess of his or her normal week's pay as a result of the payment of compensation for such holiday. To
  11|                       these ends, this section shall be administered as follows:
  12|                       Full-Time Employees (36-40 hours): The employee is entitled to each of the scheduled holidays or the equivalent time off
  13|                       with pay, based on the hourly rate of the employee for the number of hours normally worked on the day of the week on
  14|                       which the holiday falls, or for the number of hours normally worked on the day of the week given as equivalent time off, as
  15|                       the case may be.
  16|                       Part-Time Employees (minimum 20 hours): The employee is entitled to compensation for those holidays falling within his or
  17|                       her usual work schedule only, as follows:
  18|                       a. The number of hours normally scheduled for the day of week on which the holiday falls; or
  19|                       b. The number of hours normally scheduled for each week, divided by the number of days                                      normally
  20|                                scheduled to work in each week, whichever is applicable.
  21|                       Holiday time will be given on the holiday if possible. If not, where applicable, equivalent time off with pay will be granted.
  22|                        However, it according to the needs of the Department, holiday time or equivalent time off cannot be granted, the employee
  23|                       shall receive payment at one and one-half times the regular hourly rate for all hours worked on the holiday, in addition to his
  24|                       or her holiday pay. Whenever a holiday falls on Sunday, it will be observed on the Monday following. Whenever a holiday
  25|                       falls on Saturday or on a full-time employee's day off, holiday time will be scheduled by the Department Head or the
  26|                       employee will receive a Floating Holiday. The Floating Holiday is equal to eight (8) hours for employees who regularly
  27|                       work 40 hours per week, and will be prorated according to the Part-time compensation formula for those who work less than
  28|                       40 hours.       Holiday time will not be cumulative and must be taken within either three (3) weeks before or three (3) weeks
  29|                       following the specified holiday.
  30|                       SECTION 19. SICK LEAVE
  31|                        All persons employed, full-time or part-time who have completed the six (6) months probationary period by July 1 of any
  32|                       year, shall be entitled to sick leave of ninety-six (96) hours, to be credited on July 1. The part-time compensation formula
  33|                       shall be used to determine the employee's prorated sick pay (See Section 28).
  34|                       New employees having completed the six (6) months probationary period shall be credited as of the end of said six (6)
  35|                       months, with sick leave in the amount of eight (8) hours for each full month intervening between the six months anniversary
  36|                       date and the next July 1, up to the maximum of ninety-six (96) hours. Use of such leave must be occasioned by sickness or
  37|                       injury of the employee or their immediate family member.
  38|                        Unused sick leave shall be cumulative up to a maximum of 1,200 hours, and shall be carried forward on July 1 of each year,
  39|                       to be added to the sick leave credited as of July 1. Sick leave may be donated to another employee who has exhausted their
  40|                       accumulated sick leave at the discretion of the Town Manager.
  41|                        When an employee finds it necessary to be absent because of accident or illness, he/she shall report the fact to their
  42|                       immediate supervisor as soon as possible either in person or by agent. Sick leave will not be granted unless such report is
  43|                       made. For the protection of the Town, the Department Head or supervisor may require the presentation of a doctor's
  44|                       certificate in connection with a claim for sick leave that exceeds, or is equal to 24 hours (or three missed days of work), and
  45|                       may, if it is deemed advisable, send a doctor or nurse to investigate any absence alleged to be caused by illness. Any
  46|                       employee who refuses to submit to a doctor's examination shall not be entitled to sick leave.
  47|                        An employee who retires in good standing shall receive compensation based on a percentage of his/her accumulated unused
  48|                       sick leave, up to a maximum of 480 hours, as follows: 5 years continuous service 10%; 15 years continuous service 50%; 25
  49|                                                                                                    194

===PAGE 195=== (ocr, 49 lines)
   1|                       years continuous service 75%. In the event of an employee's death, the above benefit will be paid to his/her beneficiary. This
   2|                       retirement benefit will not be available to any employee hired after June 30, 2010.
   3|                       Sick Time can be used for any of the following reasons:
   4|                             • Care for the employee's own physical or mental illness, injury or medical condition that requires home care or rest,
   5|                                  professional medical diagnosis or care, or preventative medical care;
   6|                            • Care for the employee's child, spouse, parent or parent of a spouse, who is suffering from a physical or mental
   7|                                  illness, injury, or medical condition that requires home care, professional medical diagnosis or care, or preventive
   8|                                   medical care;
   9|                             • Attend the employee's routine medical appointment or a routine medical appointment for the employee's child,
  10|                                   spouse, parent, or parent of spouse.
  11|                       SECTION 20. PERSONAL LEAVE
  12|                       All persons employed, full time or part time who have completed six (6) months probationary period by July 1 of any year,
  13|                       shall be entitled to personal leave of twenty-four (24) hours, to become available on July 1 for use during the ensuing fiscal
  14|                       year. The part-time compensation formula shall be used to determine the employee's prorated personal hours (See Section
  15|                       New employees having completed the six (6) months probationary period shall be credited as of the end of said six (6)
  16|                       months, with eight (8) personal hours for use during the period between said six (6) months anniversary and the end of the
  17|                       then current fiscal year; provided, however, that the said six (6) months probationary period must have been completed by
  18|                       May 1 of that year.
  19|                       Employees who do not use any sick leave within a three month (3) month period (calculated quarterly), will be entitled to
  20|                       eight (8) additional personal hours for each such quarter; said personal hours are to be used in the same fiscal year in which
  21|                       they are earned. Personal leave shall be scheduled with the approval of the Department Head. Personal leave shall not be
  22|                       cumulative.
  23|                       SECTION 21. FAMILY AND MEDICAL LEAVE
  24|                       The Town agrees to abide by the provisions of the 1993 Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA). All eligible employees are
  25|                       entitled to up to twelve (12) weeks of unpaid leave for certain family and medical reasons in a one (1) year period.
  26|                       Employees are eligible for FMLA if they have worked for the Town for at least one (1) year and at least for one thousand two
  27|                       hundred and fifty (1,250) hours over the previous twelve (12) months.
  28|                        Unpaid FMLA leave must be granted for any of the following reasons:
  29|                       • To care for the employee's child after birth, or placement for adoption or foster care
  30|                       • To care for the employee's spouse, son, daughter, or parent, who has a serious health condition
  31|                       • For a serious health condition that makes the employee unable to perform the employee's job
  32|                       In accordance with the past practice, the Town allows, at the option of the employee, the use of paid leave time during the
  33|                       FMLA absence including accumulated Sick Leave, Vacation Leave, and Personal Leave. The Town requires all employees
  34|                       applying for an FMLA leave to notify their Department Head, in writing, thirty (30) days prior to the leave, if possible.
  35|                       SECTION 22. BEREAVEMENT LEAVE
  36|                       In the event of death in an employee's family (wife, husband, mother (in-law), father (in-law), child, grandparents, brother, or
  37|                       sister) up to and including three days off duty may be granted, with pay, not to be charged against sick leave. Any time
  38|                       above the three days is to be charged against sick leave.
  39|                       SECTION 23. MILITARY LEAVE
  40|                        Town employees with a minimum of six consecutive month's employment with the Town who serve in the State or Federal
  41|                       military training forces under orders shall be allowed full pay for not more than one normal working week and shall be
  42|                       granted a military leave of absence for the period of their required service with said forces.
  43|                       Military leave of absence with pay shall be granted to employees of the Town on occasion of their appearance before local
  44|                       draft boards or draft appeal boards, or for physical examinations ordered by said boards; but no such leave shall be granted
  45|                       for a period of more than one day without the approval of the Personnel Committee. Such leave shall be deemed to be a
  46|                       military leave of absence.
  47|                        A military leave of absence without pay shall be granted to any Town Officer or employee called to active duty with the State
  48|                       or Federal Armed Forces for purposes other than the routine annual tour of duty for training purposes.
  49|                                                                                                    195

===PAGE 196=== (ocr, 50 lines)
   1|                       As used herein, the phrases "military training forces" or "armed forces" shall mean the United States Air Force, the United
   2|                       States Army, the United States Navy, the Unites States Marine Corps, the United States Coast Guard, the Massachusetts
   3|                       National Guard, the Massachusetts Air National Guard, the Massachusetts State Guard, and any and all components thereof.
   4|                       SECTION 24. JURY DUTY
   5|                        All persons permanently employed, whether full time or part time for a minimum of twenty (20) hours per week, called for
   6|                       jury duty shall be paid by the Town, an amount equal to the difference between the compensation paid for a normal working
   7|                       period and the amount paid by the court, excluding allowance for travel, and this will be certified by the Town Clerk or
   8|                        Treasurer upon presentation of the check for monies received for Jury Duty.
   9|                       SECTION 25. LONGEVITY PAY
  10|                       After reaching ten (10) years of employment, and thereafter, each employee permanently employed, whether full or part time,
  11|                       shall receive an annual bonus equal to 2% of their annual salary, and is payable in the first pay period after July 1st
  12|                       years of continuous service - 2.5% of their annual salary, and at 20 years of continuous service - 3% of their annual salary.
  13|                       SECTION 26. TRAVEL REIMBURSEMENT
  14|                       Travel reimbursement shall be by signed voucher at a rate established by the IRS when using the employee's own car, plus
  15|                       tolls and parking fees.
  16|                       SECTION 27. DISCIPLINE POLICY
  17|                       Items which constitute grounds for disciplinary action against an employee include: chronic absenteeism or tardiness,
  18|                       insubordination or refusal to work, infraction of work and safety rules, threat of physical violence against fellow employees,
  19|                       use of profane language to a supervisor or fellow employee, or offenses of comparable gravity or severity.
  20|                       Upon determination by the Department Head that disciplinary action is warranted, the following guidelines shall be
  21|                       implemented for all employees that have successfully completed a six (6) month probationary period:
  22|                       STEP 1. 1st Offense - Written warning.
  23|                       STEP 2. 2nd Offense - A formal written reprimand notifying the employee of a one day suspension and that one further
  24|                                              offense shall result in a three day suspension without pay.
  25|                       STEP 3. 3rd Offense - Employee will receive an immediate three day suspension without pay and a written notification that
  26|                                             any further offense shall be grounds for dismissal.
  27|                       STEP 4. 4th Offense - Immediate dismissal of the employee.
  28|                       Depending on the particular circumstances, one or more of the above steps may be skipped. The offense for which
  29|                       disciplinary action is taken may be any combination of the items described above. For example, offense number one could be
  30|                       tardiness, offense number two could be absenteeism, and offense number three could be refusal to work or insubordination.
  31|                       If an employee goes twenty-four (24) months without a further offense, the first offense beyond twenty-four (24) months
  32|                       shall be disciplined at the level of step one.
  33|                       The following infractions are grounds for the immediate dismissal of an employee for just cause by the Department Head.
  34|                       Just cause may include, but shall not be limited to, the following:
  35|                       • Willful neglect or non-performance of one or more assigned duties;
  36|                       • Demonstrated incompetence in the performance of one or more assigned duties;
  37|                       • Behavior that seriously interferes with the normal operation of the municipality, the department, or any member of the
  38|                             workforce:
  39|                       • Insubordination, which shall mean a refusal to carry out a direct order;
  40|                       • Dishonesty in the performance of assigned duties:
  41|                       • Chronic absenteeism or tardiness without reasonable excuse;
  42|                       • Unauthorized possession or use of alcohol or an unprescribed controlled substance during any period of assigned work;
  43|                       • Municipal theft.
  44|                       SECTION 28. DEFINITIONS
  45|                       The following terms used in the Salary Administration Plan shall be defined as set forth herein:
  46|                       Full-Time Employee shall mean any person who spends an amount of time between thirty-six (36) and forty (40) hours of
  47|                       permanently scheduled work per week in the service of the Town.
  48|                       Hourly Employee shall mean any employee of the Town who by virtue of their classified position is compensated at an
  49|                       hourly rate for services rendered. Hourly employees are not eligible for benefits (i.e. vacation, sick-time, insurance, etc.).
  50|                                                                                                    196

===PAGE 197=== (ocr, 59 lines)
   1|                         Intermittent Employee shall mean any person who works less than twenty (20) hours per week on a regular basis.
   2|                         Intermittent employees are not eligible for benefits (i.e. vacation, sick-time, insurance, etc.) and work less than one thousand
   3|                          forty (1,040) hours per year in the service of the Town.
   4|                         Part Time Compensation Formula shall be determined by dividing the compensation or time off by 40 and then multiplying
   5|                         by the number of hours the employee works per week. For example, a 40 hour per week employee is eligible for 120 hours
   6|                         of vacation. If another employee with the same tenure works 36 hours, the formula is as follows: 120 / 40 = 3. Then
   7|                          multiply 3 x 36 hours = 108 hours.
   8|                         Part-Time Employee shall mean any person who spends less than thirty-six (36) hours but twenty (20) hours or more of
   9|                          permanently scheduled work per week in the service of the Town.
  10|                         Probationary Period shall mean the initial six (6) month period of employment with the Town.
  11|                         Seasonal Employee shall mean any employee, part or full-time who spends no more than six (6) months or one hundred
  12|                         eighty (180) days whichever is less per year, in the service of the Town. Seasonal employees are not eligible for benefits (i.e.
  13|                         vacation, sick-time, insurance, etc.).

   1|                       (Submitted by Personnel Committee) Board of Selectmen and Finance Committee recommends approval with amendments to
