   6|                       recommends approval of $6,623.00. Finance Committee recommends approval. VOTED UNANIMOUSLY to raise
   7|                       ARTICLE 15. To see if the Town will vote to adopt a Non-Binding Resolution opposing the Northeast Energy Direct
   8|                       Project as printed below; or take any other action relative thereto. (Submitted by Board of Selectmen/ Town Manager) Board
   9|                       of Selectmen recommends approval. Finance committee reports no direct financial impact.
  10|                                                       Non-Binding Resolution Opposing the Northeast Energy Direct Project
  11|                        WHEREAS, Kinder Morgan has proposed a new 36" high pressure gas pipeline through Massachusetts and New Hampshire,
  12|                       as part of a Northeast Energy Direct Project hereinafter called "the Project", and
  13|                       WHEREAS, the Project also proposes a new 12" high pressure (1460 psi) natural gas pipeline, which it calls the "Fitchburg
  14|                       Lateral", to be installed, not in Fitchburg, but in Lunenburg, Townsend, and Mason NH; and
  15|                       WHEREAS, Lunenburg is already crossed by a Kinder Morgan pipeline hereinafter called the "South Lunenburg Lateral",
  16|                       which runs from Lancaster to the proposed southern terminus of the Fitchburg Lateral; and
  17|                        WHEREAS, the South Lunenburg Lateral has already caused financial damage to Lunenburg citizens; and
  18|                        WHEREAS, the completion of the Project appears to create a connection between the proposed Fitchburg Lateral and the
  19|                       South Lunenburg Lateral; and
  20|                        WHEREAS, said connection could provide Kinder Morgan the opportunity to provide gas service to Worcester through
  21|                       Lunenburg including a possible future addition of a compressor station in Lunenburg, or other re-adaptation and re-use of the
  22|                       South Lunenburg Lateral; and
  23|                        WHEREAS, Kinder Morgan has been silent about its plans to create such a connection, despite its proposing a metering
  24|                       station in Lunenburg at the Southern terminus of the proposed Fitchburg Lateral in its Resource Report 1 filed with the
  25|                       Federal Energy Regulatory Commission; and
  26|                        WHEREAS, the currently proposed pipeline route was chosen in a private, closed process so that there has been no chance
  27|                       for open, public discussion or debate of alternate routing possibilities and tradeoffs; and
  28|                       WHEREAS, Kinder Morgan identified properties in Lunenburg that it intends the Fitchburg Lateral to cross but declined to
  29|                       provide the town of Lunenburg with detailed and current information on the exact route it is proposing; and
  30|                       WHEREAS, landowners are being asked to permit surveying on their property or to sign agreements to forfeit some of their
  31|                       property rights; and
  32|                        WHEREAS, federal eminent domain powers may be used to forcibly take pipeline easements from unwilling landowners;
  33|                       WHEREAS, a high-pressure gas pipeline, by its nature, carries the potential for leak, rupture or devastating explosion
  34|                       causing untold damage to property and lives; and
  35|                        WHEREAS, said pipeline goes against current Massachusetts commitments to renewable energies and combating global
  36|                       climate change; and
  37|                        WHEREAS, our energy challenges are better addressed through investment in energy conservation measures as well as green
  38|                       and renewable energy solutions; and
  39|                        WHEREAS, Lunenburg and our neighboring communities have adopted comprehensive master plans, zoning bylaws,
  40|                       wetlands bylaws and other land use controls to provide for the orderly development of our communities and the conservation
  41|                       and protection of our communities for future generations to come, as good stewards of the land should; and
  42|                        WHEREAS, the elimination of environmental threats to our forests and streams from improvident developments is the
  43|                       fundamental purpose for the adoption of our land use controls and master plans; and
  44|                        WHEREAS, Lunenburg and our neighboring communities have publicly and privately set aside large tracts of land and
  45|                       restricted their development for conservation and open space purposes as part of their master plans;
  46|                       NOW, THEREFORE, be it RESOLVED that the Town of Lunenburg does hereby declare that it:
  47|                       STANDS IN OPPOSITION to Kinder Morgan's proposed Energy Direct Project and to the Fitchburg Lateral; and
  48|                       STANDS IN OPPOSITION to any effort to locate the proposed Fitchburg Lateral within Lunenburg's borders; and
  49|                                                                                                    199

===PAGE 200=== (ocr, 9 lines)
   1|                       FURTHER COMMITS to participate in and provide comments to any meetings held under the Federal Energy Regulatory
   2|                        Commission (FERC) review process with regard to the proposed Fitchburg Lateral to oppose Kinder Morgan's application;
   3|                       and
   4|                        BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Town of Lunenburg does hereby call upon its state and federal legislators and
   5|                       Executive branch officers to enact legislation and take any such other actions as are necessary to oppose such energy projects
   6|                       that go against our commitment to public safety, our environment, our economic well-being and our sense of community.
   7|                       VOTED
